#!/bin/bash
# ============================================================================
# Session launcher - TUI menu for starting desktop sessions from TTY
# ============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

# ── Colors & Drawing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Gruvbox-inspired palette
C_BG="\033[48;5;235m"       # dark bg
C_FG="\033[38;5;223m"       # light fg
C_DIM="\033[38;5;245m"      # dimmed
C_ACCENT="\033[38;5;214m"   # orange accent
C_ACCENT2="\033[38;5;142m"  # green accent
C_ACCENT3="\033[38;5;109m"  # blue accent
C_ACCENT4="\033[38;5;175m"  # purple accent
C_SEL_BG="\033[48;5;237m"   # selected bg
C_SEL_FG="\033[38;5;214m"   # selected fg
C_BOLD="\033[1m"
C_RESET="\033[0m"
C_HIDE="\033[?25l"
C_SHOW="\033[?25h"
C_CLEAR="\033[2J\033[H"

# Box drawing
H="─"  V="│"  TL="╭"  TR="╮"  BL="╰"  BR="╯"

# ── Session definitions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Format: "id|name|description|type|command"
#   type: wayland, x11, script

SESSIONS=(
    "somewm|somewm|Wayland compositor (wlroots)|wayland|somewm-session"
    "kde|KDE Plasma|Wayland desktop environment|wayland|/usr/lib/plasma-dbus-run-session-if-needed /usr/bin/startplasma-wayland"
    "awesome|AwesomeWM|X11 window manager (via .xinitrc)|x11|$HOME/.xinitrc awesome"
    "hyprland|Hyprland|Wayland compositor (wlroots)|wayland|dbus-run-session Hyprland"
)

# Filter to only sessions whose binary exists
AVAILABLE=()
for entry in "${SESSIONS[@]}"; do
    IFS='|' read -r id name desc type cmd <<< "$entry"
    # Check first word of command
    local_bin="${cmd%% *}"
    if command -v "$local_bin" &>/dev/null || [ -x "$local_bin" ]; then
        AVAILABLE+=("$entry")
    fi
done

if [ ${#AVAILABLE[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "No sessions available."
    exit 1
fi

# ── Drawing functions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

get_term_size() {
    LINES=$(tput lines)
    COLS=$(tput cols)
}

# Print at position
at() { printf "\033[%d;%dH" "$1" "$2"; }

# Draw horizontal line
hline() {
    local y=$1 x=$2 len=$3 color=${4:-$C_DIM}
    at "$y" "$x"
    printf "%b" "$color"
    printf "%0.s$H" $(seq 1 "$len")
    printf "%b" "$C_RESET"
}

# Draw box
box() {
    local y=$1 x=$2 w=$3 h=$4 color=${5:-$C_DIM}
    at "$y" "$x"; printf "%b%s" "$color" "$TL"
    printf "%0.s$H" $(seq 1 $((w-2)))
    printf "%s%b" "$TR" "$C_RESET"

    for ((i=1; i<h-1; i++)); do
        at $((y+i)) "$x"; printf "%b%s%b" "$color" "$V" "$C_RESET"
        at $((y+i)) $((x+w-1)); printf "%b%s%b" "$color" "$V" "$C_RESET"
    done

    at $((y+h-1)) "$x"; printf "%b%s" "$color" "$BL"
    printf "%0.s$H" $(seq 1 $((w-2)))
    printf "%s%b" "$BR" "$C_RESET"
}

# Center text in given width
center() {
    local text="$1" width=$2
    local len=${#text}
    local pad=$(( (width - len) / 2 ))
    printf "%*s%s%*s" "$pad" "" "$text" $((width - len - pad)) ""
}

# ── ASCII Art ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

draw_logo() {
    local y=$1 x=$2
    local O=$'\033[38;5;214m'   # orange (sloth)
    local B=$'\033[38;5;172m'   # brown (nose)
    local W=$'\033[38;5;223m'   # warm white (face)
    local D=$'\033[38;5;239m'   # dim (feet)
    local R=$'\033[0m'

    local -a lines=()
    lines+=("${W}   --(( ${W}----${W} ))--${R}")
    lines+=("${O}      \\\\     /|${R}")
    lines+=("${W}   p${B}*${W}q${O}/  \\_/  \\\\${R}")
    lines+=("${O}   \\\\          /${R}")
    lines+=("${O}    \" _     _\"${R}")
    lines+=("${O}        —  —${R}")
    local i=0
    for line in "${lines[@]}"; do
        at $((y + i)) "$x"
        printf "%s" "$line"
        ((i+=1))
    done

    # Motto centered independently
    local motto="\"Chces slyset vtip, Blesku?\""
    at $((y + i + 1)) $(( x - 3 ))
    printf "%s" "${D}${motto}${R}"
}

draw_wm_name() {
    local y=$1 x=$2 id=$3
    local A=$'\033[38;5;214m'
    local R=$'\033[0m'

    local -a art=()
    case "$id" in
        somewm)
            art+=(' ___  ___  _ __ ___   _____      ___ __ ___  ')
            art+=('/ __|/ _ \| '"'"'_ ` _ \ / _ \ \ /\ / / '"'"'_ ` _ \ ')
            art+=('\__ \ (_) | | | | | |  __/\ V  V /| | | | | |')
            art+=('|___/\___/|_| |_| |_|\___| \_/\_/ |_| |_| |_|')
            ;;
        kde)
            art+=(' _  _____  ___   ___ _                    ')
            art+=('| |/ /   \| __| | _ \ |__ _ ____ __  __ _ ')
            art+=('| '"'"' <| |) | _|  |  _/ / _` (_-< '"'"'  \/ _` |')
            art+=('|_|\_\___/|___| |_| |_\__,_/__/_|_|_\__,_|')
            ;;
        awesome)
            art+=('   _                             __      ____  __ ')
            art+=('  /_\__ __ _____ ___ ___ _ __  __\ \    / /  \/  |')
            art+=(' / _ \ V  V / -_|_-</ _ \ '"'"'  \/ -_) \/\/ /| |\/| |')
            art+=('/_/ \_\_/\_/\___/__/\___/_|_|_\___|\_/\_/ |_|  |_|')
            ;;
        hyprland)
            art+=(' _  _               _              _ ')
            art+=('| || |_  _ _ __ _ _| |__ _ _ _  __| |')
            art+=('| __ | || | '"'"'_ \ '"'"'_| / _` | '"'"' \/ _` |')
            art+=('|_||_|\_, | .__/_| |_\__,_|_||_\__,_|')
            art+=('      |__/|_|                        ')
            ;;
    esac

    local i=0
    for line in "${art[@]}"; do
        at $((y + i)) "$x"
        printf "%s%s%s" "$A" "$line" "$R"
        ((i+=1))
    done
}

draw_system_info() {
    local y=$1 x=$2 w=$3
    local kernel hostname uptime_str mem_str

    kernel=$(uname -r | sed 's/-.*//')
    hostname=$(uname -n)
    uptime_str=$(uptime -p 2>/dev/null | sed 's/up //' || echo "?")
    mem_str=$(free -h 2>/dev/null | awk '/Mem:/{print $3"/"$2}' || echo "?")

    at "$y" "$x"
    printf "%b%b%s%b  %b%s%b  %b%s%b  %b%s%b" \
        "$C_DIM" \
        "$C_ACCENT3" "⬡ $hostname" "$C_DIM" \
        "$C_ACCENT2" "⚙ $kernel" "$C_DIM" \
        "$C_ACCENT4" "↑ $uptime_str" "$C_DIM" \
        "$C_ACCENT" "▪ $mem_str" "$C_RESET"
}

# ── Menu ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

draw_menu() {
    local selected=$1
    local box_w=56
    local box_x=$(( (COLS - box_w) / 2 ))
    local box_y=20
    local item_count=${#AVAILABLE[@]}
    local box_h=$(( item_count * 3 + 4 ))

    # Box
    box "$box_y" "$box_x" "$box_w" "$box_h" "$C_DIM"

    # Title
    at "$box_y" $((box_x + 2))
    printf "%b%b %s %b" "$C_DIM" "$C_BOLD$C_ACCENT" "SELECT SESSION" "$C_RESET"

    # Items
    local idx=0
    for entry in "${AVAILABLE[@]}"; do
        IFS='|' read -r id name desc type cmd <<< "$entry"
        local iy=$((box_y + 2 + idx * 3))

        # Type badge
        local badge badge_color
        case "$type" in
            wayland) badge="WL"  ; badge_color="$C_ACCENT2";;
            x11)     badge="X11" ; badge_color="$C_ACCENT4";;
            script)  badge="SH"  ; badge_color="$C_ACCENT3";;
        esac

        if [ "$idx" -eq "$selected" ]; then
            # Selected item - highlighted
            at "$iy" $((box_x + 2))
            printf "%b%b  ▸ %b%-20s %b[%s]%b" \
                "$C_SEL_BG" "$C_SEL_FG" "$C_BOLD" "$name" "$badge_color" "$badge" "$C_RESET"
            at $((iy + 1)) $((box_x + 2))
            printf "%b%b    %-48s%b" \
                "$C_SEL_BG" "$C_FG" "$desc" "$C_RESET"
        else
            # Normal item
            at "$iy" $((box_x + 2))
            printf "%b    %-20s %b[%s]%b" \
                "$C_DIM" "$name" "$badge_color" "$badge" "$C_RESET"
            at $((iy + 1)) $((box_x + 2))
            printf "%b    %-48s%b" \
                "\033[38;5;241m" "$desc" "$C_RESET"
        fi

        ((idx+=1))
    done

    # Footer
    local footer_y=$((box_y + box_h))
    at "$footer_y" "$box_x"
    printf "%b  ↑↓ navigate  ⏎ launch  q quit%b" "$C_DIM" "$C_RESET"
}

# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cleanup() {
    printf "%b%b" "$C_SHOW" "$C_RESET"
    tput cnorm 2>/dev/null
    stty sane 2>/dev/null
    clear
}
trap cleanup EXIT

main() {
    get_term_size

    # Hide cursor
    printf "%b%b" "$C_HIDE" "$C_CLEAR"

    local selected=0
    local item_count=${#AVAILABLE[@]}

    while true; do
        # Clear and draw
        printf "%b" "$C_CLEAR"

        # Logo centered
        local logo_w=30
        local logo_x=$(( (COLS - logo_w) / 2 ))
        draw_logo 2 "$logo_x"

        # WM name ASCII art (below motto)
        local sel_entry="${AVAILABLE[$selected]}"
        local sel_id
        IFS='|' read -r sel_id _ _ _ _ <<< "$sel_entry"
        local wm_art_w=52
        draw_wm_name 12 $(( (COLS - wm_art_w) / 2 )) "$sel_id"

        # System info
        draw_system_info 18 $(( (COLS - 60) / 2 )) 60

        # Menu
        draw_menu "$selected"

        # Read key (bash read -rsn1 works on both TTY and pty)
        local key
        IFS= read -rsn1 key

        case "$key" in
            $'\x1b')
                # Escape sequence - read remaining bytes with timeout
                # Arrow keys send \x1b[A etc. Bare Escape = nothing follows
                local seq
                IFS= read -rsn2 -t 0.1 seq || true
                case "$seq" in
                    "[A") # Up
                        selected=$(( (selected - 1 + item_count) % item_count ))
                        ;;
                    "[B") # Down
                        selected=$(( (selected + 1) % item_count ))
                        ;;
                    "") # Bare Escape (no follow-up bytes)
                        exit 0
                        ;;
                esac
                ;;
            "") # Enter
                # Launch selected session
                local entry="${AVAILABLE[$selected]}"
                IFS='|' read -r id name desc type cmd <<< "$entry"

                # Restore terminal
                cleanup
                trap - EXIT

                echo "Launching $name..."
                sleep 0.3

                case "$type" in
                    x11)
                        exec startx $cmd
                        ;;
                    wayland|script)
                        exec $cmd
                        ;;
                esac
                ;;
            "q"|"Q") # Quit
                exit 0
                ;;
            "k") # vim up
                selected=$(( (selected - 1 + item_count) % item_count ))
                ;;
            "j") # vim down
                selected=$(( (selected + 1) % item_count ))
                ;;
        esac
    done
}

agetty specifies a ":" delimited list of files and directories to be displayed instead of /etc/issue. All specified files and directories are displayed, missing or empty files are silently ignored. # agetty Escape Codes Reference

Based on the manual page, here are the escape codes supported in `/etc/issue` files:

## Available Escape Codes

| Code | Function |
|------|----------|
| `\4` or `\4{interface}` | "Insert the IPv4 address of the specified network interface" |
| `\6` or `\6{interface}` | IPv6 equivalent of `\4` |
| `\b` | "Insert the baudrate of the current line" |
| `\d` | "Insert the current date" |
| `\e` or `\e{name}` | Translates human-readable color names to escape sequences (e.g., `\e{red}`) |
| `\s` | "Insert the system name (the name of the operating system)" |
| `\S` or `\S{VARIABLE}` | Retrieves data from `/etc/os-release` or `/usr/lib/os-release` |
| `\l` | "Insert the name of the current tty line" |
| `\m` | "Insert the architecture identifier of the machine" |
| `\n` | "Insert the nodename of the machine, also known as the hostname" |
| `\o` | "Insert the NIS domainname of the machine" |
| `\O` | "Insert the DNS domainname of the machine" |
| `\r` | "Insert the release number of the OS" |
| `\t` | "Insert the current time" |
| `\u` | "Insert the number of current users logged in" |
| `\U` | "Insert the string '1 user' or '<n> users'" |
| `\v` | "Insert the version of the OS, that is, the build-date and such" |

## ANSI Color Support

The `\e{name}` code supports these color names: black, blue, cyan, green, magenta, red, yellow, white, plus variants like lightblue, darkgray, and special codes like bold, blink, and reset.

**Note:** The manual contains no information about `/etc/motd` or its escape codes.

content.text:
Ano, přesně tak. JimmyCozza napsal, že vytvořil skript s 10 000 notifikacemi za 24 hodin a žádná se nezasekla. Ty jsi mu pak odpověděl, že se to děje konkrétně, když přijde víc Google Calendar událostí najednou — poslední se pravidelně zasekne.

Takže problém je nejspíš v tom, že notifikace přicházejí **paralelně ve stejný okamžik** (race condition), ne sekvenčně. Jeho test s postupným posíláním to neodhalí.

Chceš, abych se na to podíval blíž? Mohl bych prozkoumat naughty kód a zkusit najít ten race condition, nebo napsat reprodukční skript, který posílá notifikace skutečně paralelně.

1→---------------------------------------------------------------------------

     3→--
     4→-- @author Uli Schlachter <psychon@znc.in>
     5→-- @copyright 2014 Uli Schlachter
     6→-- @module naughty
     7→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     8→
     9→local naughty = require("naughty.core")
    10→local gdebug = require("gears.debug")
    11→local capi = {awesome = awesome, screen = screen}
    12→if dbus then
    13→    naughty.dbus = require("naughty.dbus")
    14→end
    15→
    16→naughty.action = require("naughty.action")
    17→naughty.list = require("naughty.list")
    18→naughty.layout = require("naughty.layout")
    19→naughty.widget = require("naughty.widget")
    20→naughty.container = require("naughty.container")
    21→naughty.action = require("naughty.action")
    22→naughty.notification = require("naughty.notification")
    23→
    24→-- Attempt to handle early errors when using the manual screen mode.
    25→--
    26→-- Creating a notification popup before the screens are added won't work. To
    27→-- work around this, the code below initializes some screens. One potential
    28→-- problem is that it could emit enough signal to cause even more errors and
    29→-- lose the original error.
    30→--
    31→-- For example, the following error can be displayed using this fallback:
    32→--
    33→--    screen.connect_signal("scanned", function() foobar() end)
    34→--
    35→local function screen_fallback()
    36→    if capi.screen.count() == 0 then
    37→        gdebug.print_warning("An error occurred before a screen was added")
    38→
    39→        -- Private API to scan for screens now.
    40→        if #screen._viewports() == 0 then
    41→            screen._scan_quiet()
    42→        end
    43→
    44→        local viewports = screen._viewports()
    45→
    46→        if #viewports > 0 then
    47→            for _, viewport in ipairs(viewports) do
    48→                local geo = viewport.geometry
    49→                local s = capi.screen.fake_add(geo.x, geo.y, geo.width, geo.height)
    50→                s.outputs = viewport.outputs
    51→            end
    52→        else
    53→            capi.screen.fake_add(0, 0, 640, 480)
    54→        end
    55→    end
    56→end
    57→
    58→-- Handle runtime errors during startup
    59→if capi.awesome.startup_errors then
    60→
    61→    -- Wait until `rc.lua` is executed before creating the notifications.
    62→    -- Otherwise nothing is handling them (yet).
    63→    client.connect_signal("scanning", function()
    64→        -- A lot of things have to go wrong for this to happen, but it can.
    65→        screen_fallback()
    66→
    67→        naughty.emit_signal(
    68→            "request::display_error", capi.awesome.startup_errors, true
    69→        )
    70→    end)
    71→end
    72→
    73→-- Handle runtime errors after startup
    74→do
    75→    local in_error = false
    76→
    77→    capi.awesome.connect_signal("debug::error", function (err)
    78→        -- Make sure we don't go into an endless error loop
    79→        if in_error then return end
    80→
    81→        in_error = true
    82→
    83→        screen_fallback()
    84→
    85→        naughty.emit_signal("request::display_error", tostring(err), false)
    86→
    87→        in_error = false
    88→    end)
    89→
    90→end
    91→
    92→return naughty
    93→

   365→--- Destroy all notifications on given screens.

   368→-- destroyed. If nil, destroy notifications on all screens.

   372→-- otherwise.

   374→-- @staticfct naughty.destroy_all_notifications
   375→function naughty.destroy_all_notifications(screens, reason)
   376→    if not screens then
   377→        screens = {}
   378→        for key, _ in pairs(naughty.notifications) do

   382→    local ret = true
   383→    for _, scr in pairs(screens) do

   385→            while #list > 0 do

   388→
   389→                ret = ret and list[1]:destroy(reason)
   390→            end
   391→        end
   392→    end

   394→end

   479→-- Remove the notification from the internal list(s)
   480→local function cleanup(self, reason)
   481→    assert(reason, "Use n:destroy() instead of emitting the signal directly")
   482→
   483→    if properties.suspended then
   484→        for k, v in ipairs(naughty.notifications.suspended) do
   485→            if v == self then
   486→                table.remove(naughty.notifications.suspended, k)
   487→                break
   488→            end
   489→        end
   490→    end
   491→    local scr = self.screen
   492→
   493→    assert(naughty.notifications[scr][self.position][self.idx] == self)
   494→    remove_from_index(self)
   495→
   496→    -- Update all indices
   497→    for k, n in ipairs(naughty.notifications[scr][self.position]) do
   498→        n.idx = k
   499→    end
   500→
   501→    -- Remove from the global active list.
   502→    for k, n in ipairs(naughty._active) do
   503→         if n == self then
   504→            table.remove(naughty._active, k)
   505→            naughty.emit_signal("property::active")
   506→         end
   507→    end
   508→
   509→    -- `self.timer.started` will be false if the expiration was paused.
   510→    if self.timer and self.timer.started then
   511→        self.timer:stop()
   512→    end
   513→
   514→    if self.destroy_cb and reason ~= naughty.notification_closed_reason.silent then
   515→        self.destroy_cb(reason or naughty.notification_closed_reason.undefined)
   516→    end
   517→end
   518→
   519→naughty.connect_signal("destroyed", cleanup)

   631→-- network URLs, AwesomeWM will not attempt to load it. If you wish to see the
   632→-- icon displayed, you must provide an handler. It is highly recommended for
   633→-- handler to only set `n.icon` when they *found* the icon. That way multiple

   637→-- only supports one if them, it should check the `context` and return if it

   643→-- * image

   648→-- icon lookup will look like:
   649→--
   650→--    naughty.connect_signal("request::icon", function(n, context, hints)
   651→--        if context ~= "app_icon" then return end
   652→--

   655→--

   657→--            n.icon = path
   658→--        end
   659→--    end)

   662→-- handle animations. This is not supported by default.

   675→-- @signal request::screen
   676→-- @tparam table notification The `naughty.notification` object. This is
   677→--  currently either "new" or "removed".
   678→-- @tparam string context Why is the signal sent.
   679→
   680→-- Register a new notification object.
   681→local function register(notification, args)
   682→    assert(not notification._private.registered)
   683→
   684→    -- Add the some more properties
   685→    rawset(notification, "get_suspended", get_suspended)
   686→
   687→    local s = get_screen(notification.screen or args.screen
   688→        or (notification.preset and notification.preset.screen))
   689→
   690→    if not s then
   691→        naughty.emit_signal("request::screen", notification, "new", {})
   692→        s = notification.screen
   693→    end
   694→
   695→    assert(s)
   696→
   697→    if not naughty.notifications[s] then
   698→        init_screen(get_screen(s))
   699→    end
   700→
   701→    -- insert the notification to the table
   702→    table.insert(naughty._active, notification)
   703→    table.insert(naughty.notifications[s][notification.position], notification)
   704→    notification.idx    = #naughty.notifications[s][notification.position]
   705→    notification.screen = s
   706→
   707→    notification._private.registered = true
   708→
   709→    notification._private.args = args
   710→
   711→    if properties.suspended and not args.ignore_suspend then
   712→        table.insert(naughty.notifications.suspended, notification)
   713→    else
   714→        naughty.emit_signal("added", notification, args)
   715→    end
   716→
   717→    assert(rawget(notification, "preset") or naughty._has_preset_handler)
   718→
   719→    naughty.emit_signal("property::active")
   720→
   721→    -- return the notification
   722→    return notification
   723→end
   724→
   725→naughty.connect_signal("new", register)
   726→
   727→local function index_miss(_, key)
   728→    if rawget(naughty, "get_"..key) then
   729→         return rawget(naughty, "get_"..key)()
   730→    elseif properties[key] ~= nil then
   731→        return properties[key]
   732→    else
   733→        return nil
   734→    end
   735→end
   736→
   737→local function set_index_miss(_, key, value)
   738→    if rawget(naughty, "set_"..key) then
   739→         return rawget(naughty, "set_"..key)(value)
   740→    elseif properties[key] ~= nil then
   741→        assert(type(value) == "boolean")
   742→        properties[key] = value
   743→
   744→        naughty.emit_signal("property::"..key, value)
   745→    else
   746→        rawset(naughty, key, value)
   747→    end
   748→end
   749→
   750→--- Create a notification.
   751→--
   752→-- This function is deprecated, create notification objects instead:
   753→--
   754→--    local notif = naughty.notification(args)
   755→--
   756→-- @tparam table args The argument table containing any of the arguments below.
   757→-- @string[opt=""] args.text Text of the notification.
   758→-- @string[opt] args.title Title of the notification.
   759→-- @int[opt=5] args.timeout Time in seconds after which popup expires.
   760→--   Set 0 for no timeout.
   761→-- @int[opt] args.hover_timeout Delay in seconds after which hovered popup disappears.
   762→-- @tparam[opt=awful.screen.focused()] integer|screen args.screen Target screen for the notification.
   763→-- @string[opt="top_right"] args.position Corner of the workarea displaying the popups.
   764→--   Values: `"top_right"`, `"top_left"`, `"bottom_left"`,
   765→--   `"bottom_right"`, `"top_middle"`, `"bottom_middle"`, `"middle"`.
   766→-- @bool[opt=true] args.ontop Boolean forcing popups to display on top.
   767→-- @int[opt=`beautiful.notification_height` or auto] args.height Popup height.
   768→-- @int[opt=`beautiful.notification_width` or auto] args.width Popup width.
   769→-- @string[opt=`beautiful.notification_font` or `beautiful.font` or `awesome.font`] args.font Notification font.
   770→-- @string[opt] args.icon Path to icon.
   771→-- @int[opt] args.icon_size Desired icon size in px.
   772→-- @string[opt=`beautiful.notification_fg` or `beautiful.fg_focus` or `'#ffffff'`] args.fg Foreground color.
   773→-- @string[opt=`beautiful.notification_fg` or `beautiful.bg_focus` or `'#535d6c'`] args.bg Background color.
   774→-- @int[opt=`beautiful.notification_border_width` or 1] args.border_width Border width.
   775→-- @string[opt=`beautiful.notification_border_color` or `beautiful.border_color_active` or `'#535d6c'`] args.border_color Border color.
   776→-- @tparam[opt=`beautiful.notification_shape`] gears.shape args.shape Widget shape.
   777→-- @tparam[opt=`beautiful.notification_opacity`] gears.opacity args.opacity Widget opacity.
   778→-- @tparam[opt=`beautiful.notification_margin`] gears.margin args.margin Widget margin.
   779→-- @tparam[opt] function args.run Function to run on left click.  The notification
   780→--   object will be passed to it as an argument.
   781→--   You need to call e.g.
   782→--   `notification.die(naughty.notification_closed_reason.dismissedByUser)` from
   783→--   there to dismiss the notification yourself.
   784→-- @tparam[opt] function args.destroy Function to run when notification is destroyed.
   785→-- @tparam[opt] table args.preset Table with any of the above parameters.
   786→--   Note: Any parameters specified directly in args will override ones defined
   787→--   in the preset.
   788→-- @tparam[opt] integer args.replaces_id Replace the notification with the given ID.
   789→-- @tparam[opt] function args.callback Function that will be called with all arguments.
   790→--   The notification will only be displayed if the function returns true.
   791→--   Note: this function is only relevant to notifications sent via dbus.
   792→-- @tparam[opt] table args.actions A list of `naughty.action`s.
   793→-- @bool[opt=false] args.ignore_suspend If set to true this notification
   794→--   will be shown even if notifications are suspended via `naughty.suspend`.
   795→-- @usage naughty.notify({ title = "Achtung!", message = "You're idling", timeout = 0 })
   796→-- @treturn ?table The notification object, or nil in case a notification was
   797→--   not displayed.
   798→-- @deprecated naughty.notify
   799→
   800→local nnotif = nil
   801→
   802→function naughty.notify(args)
   803→    gdebug.deprecate(
   804→        "Use local notif = naughty.notification(args)",
   805→        {deprecated_in=5}
   806→    )
   807→
   808→    --TODO v6 remove this hack
   809→    nnotif = nnotif or require("naughty.notification")
   810→
   811→    -- The existing notification object, if any.
   812→    local n = args and args.replaces_id and
   813→        naughty.get_by_id(args.replaces_id) or nil
   814→
   815→    -- It was possible to update the notification content using `replaces_id`.
   816→    -- This is a concept that come from the dbus API and leaked into the public
   817→    -- API. It has all kind of issues and brokenness, but it being used.
   818→    if n then
   819→        return gtable.crush(n, args)
   820→    end
   821→
   822→    return nnotif(args)
   823→end
   824→
   825→--- Request handler to get the icon using the clients icons.
   826→-- @signalhandler naughty.client_icon_handler
   827→function naughty.client_icon_handler(self, context)
   828→    if context ~= "clients" then return end
   829→
   830→    local clients = self:get_clients()
   831→
   832→    for _, t in ipairs { "normal", "dialog" } do
   833→        for _, c in ipairs(clients) do
   834→            if c.type == t then
   835→                self._private.icon = gsurface(c.icon) --TODO support other size
   836→                return
   837→            end
   838→        end
   839→    end
   840→end
   841→
   842→--- Request handler to get the icon using the image or path.
   843→-- @signalhandler naughty.icon_path_handler
   844→function naughty.icon_path_handler(self, context, hints)
   845→    if context ~= "image" and context ~= "path" then return end
   846→
   847→    self._private.icon = gsurface.load_uncached_silently(
   848→        hints.path or hints.image
   849→    )
   850→end
   851→
   852→--- Request handler for clearing the icon when asked by ie, DBus.
   853→-- @signalhandler naughty.icon_clear_handler
   854→function naughty.icon_clear_handler(self, context, hints) --luacheck: no unused args
   855→    if context ~= "dbus_clear" then return end
   856→
   857→    self._private.icon = nil
   858→    self:emit_signal("property::icon")
   859→end
   860→
   861→naughty.connect_signal("property::screen"  , update_index)
   862→naughty.connect_signal("property::position", update_index)
   863→
   864→naughty.connect_signal("request::icon", naughty.client_icon_handler)
   865→naughty.connect_signal("request::icon", naughty.icon_path_handler  )
   866→naughty.connect_signal("request::icon", naughty.icon_clear_handler )
   867→
   868→--@DOC_signals_COMMON@
   869→
   870→return setmetatable(naughty, {__index = index_miss, __newindex = set_index_miss})
   871→

1→----------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→--- A notification popup widget.
     3→--
     4→-- By default, the box is composed of many other widgets:
     5→--
     6→--@DOC_wibox_nwidget_default_EXAMPLE@
     7→--
     8→-- @author Emmanuel Lepage Vallee <elv1313@gmail.com>
     9→-- @copyright 2017 Emmanuel Lepage Vallee
    10→-- @popupmod naughty.layout.box
    11→-- @supermodule awful.popup
    12→----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    13→
    14→local capi       = {screen=screen}
    15→local beautiful  = require("beautiful")
    16→local gtimer     = require("gears.timer")
    17→local gtable     = require("gears.table")
    18→local wibox      = require("wibox")
    19→local popup      = require("awful.popup")
    20→local awcommon   = require("awful.widget.common")
    21→local placement  = require("awful.placement")
    22→local abutton    = require("awful.button")
    23→local ascreen    = require("awful.screen")
    24→local gpcall     = require("gears.protected_call")
    25→local dpi        = require("beautiful").xresources.apply_dpi
    26→local cst        = require("naughty.constants")
    27→
    28→local default_widget = require("naughty.widget._default")
    29→
    30→local box, by_position = {}, {}
    31→
    32→-- Init the weak tables for each positions. It is done ahead of time rather
    33→-- than when notifications are added to simplify the code.
    34→
    35→local function init_screen(s)
    36→    if not s.valid then return end
    37→
    38→    if by_position[s] then return by_position[s] end
    39→
    40→    by_position[s] = setmetatable({},{__mode = "k"})
    41→
    42→    for _, pos in ipairs { "top_left"   , "top_middle"   , "top_right",
    43→                           "bottom_left", "bottom_middle", "bottom_right" } do
    44→        by_position[s][pos] = setmetatable({},{__mode = "v"})
    45→    end
    46→
    47→    return by_position[s]
    48→end
    49→
    50→local function disconnect(self)
    51→    local n = self._private.notification[1]
    52→
    53→    if n then
    54→        n:disconnect_signal("destroyed",
    55→            self._private.destroy_callback)
    56→
    57→        n:disconnect_signal("property::margin",
    58→            self._private.update)
    59→
    60→        n:disconnect_signal("property::suspended",
    61→            self._private.hide)
    62→    end
    63→end
    64→
    65→ascreen.connect_for_each_screen(init_screen)
    66→
    67→-- Manually cleanup to help the GC.
    68→capi.screen.connect_signal("removed", function(scr)
    69→    -- By that time, all direct events should have been handled. Cleanup the
    70→    -- leftover. Being a weak table doesn't help Lua 5.1.
    71→    gtimer.delayed_call(function()
    72→        by_position[scr] = nil
    73→    end)
    74→end)
    75→
    76→local function get_spacing()
    77→    local margin = beautiful.notification_spacing or dpi(2)
    78→    return {top = margin, bottom = margin}
    79→end
    80→
    81→local function get_offset(position, preset)
    82→    preset = preset or {}
    83→    local margin = preset.padding or beautiful.notification_spacing or dpi(4)
    84→    if position:match('_right') then
    85→        return {x = -margin}
    86→    elseif position:match('_left') then
    87→        return {x = margin}
    88→    end
    89→    return {}
    90→end
    91→
    92→-- Leverage `awful.placement` to create the stacks.
    93→local function update_position(position, preset)
    94→    local pref  = position:match("top_") and "bottom" or "top"
    95→    local align = position:match("_(.*)")
    96→        :gsub("left", "front"):gsub("right", "back")
    97→
    98→    for _, pos in pairs(by_position) do
    99→        for k, wdg in ipairs(pos[position]) do
   100→            local args = {
   101→                geometry            = pos[position][k-1],
   102→                preferred_positions = {pref },
   103→                preferred_anchors   = {align},
   104→                margins             = get_spacing(),
   105→                honor_workarea      = true,
   106→            }
   107→            if k == 1 then
   108→                args.offset = get_offset(position, preset)
   109→            end
   110→
   111→            -- The first entry is aligned to the workarea, then the following to the
   112→            -- previous widget.
   113→            placement[k==1 and position:gsub("_middle", "") or "next_to"](wdg, args)
   114→        end
   115→    end
   116→end
   117→
   118→local function finish(self)
   119→    self.visible = false
   120→    assert(init_screen(self.screen)[self.position])
   121→
   122→    for k, v in ipairs(init_screen(self.screen)[self.position]) do
   123→        if v == self then
   124→            table.remove(init_screen(self.screen)[self.position], k)
   125→            break
   126→        end
   127→    end
   128→
   129→    local preset = (self._private.notification[1] or {}).preset
   130→
   131→    update_position(self.position, preset)
   132→
   133→    disconnect(self)
   134→
   135→    self._private.notification = {}
   136→end
   137→
   138→-- It isn't a good idea to use the `attach` `awful.placement` property. If the
   139→-- screen is resized or the notification is moved, it causes side effects.
   140→-- Better listen to geometry changes and reflow.
   141→capi.screen.connect_signal("property::geometry", function(s)
   142→    for pos, notifs in pairs(by_position[s]) do
   143→        if #notifs > 0 then
   144→            update_position(pos, notifs[1].preset)
   145→        end
   146→    end
   147→end)
   148→
   149→--- The maximum notification width.
   150→-- @beautiful beautiful.notification_max_width
   151→-- @tparam[opt=500] number notification_max_width
   152→
   153→--- The maximum notification position.
   154→--
   155→-- Valid values are:
   156→--
   157→-- * top_left
   158→-- * top_middle
   159→-- * top_right
   160→-- * bottom_left
   161→-- * bottom_middle
   162→-- * bottom_right
   163→--
   164→-- @beautiful beautiful.notification_position
   165→-- @tparam[opt="top_right"] string notification_position
   166→
   167→--- The widget notification object.
   168→--
   169→-- @property notification
   170→-- @tparam naughty.notification notification
   171→-- @propertydefault This must be provided by the constructor.
   172→-- @propemits true false
   173→
   174→--- The widget template to construct the box content.
   175→--
   176→--@DOC_wibox_nwidget_default_EXAMPLE@
   177→--
   178→-- The default template is (less or more):
   179→--
   180→--    {
   181→--        {
   182→--            {
   183→--                {
   184→--                    {
   185→--                        naughty.widget.icon,
   186→--                        {
   187→--                            naughty.widget.title,
   188→--                            naughty.widget.message,
   189→--                            spacing = 4,
   190→--                            layout  = wibox.layout.fixed.vertical,
   191→--                        },
   192→--                        fill_space = true,
   193→--                        spacing    = 4,
   194→--                        layout     = wibox.layout.fixed.horizontal,
   195→--                    },
   196→--                    naughty.list.actions,
   197→--                    spacing = 10,
   198→--                    layout  = wibox.layout.fixed.vertical,
   199→--                },
   200→--                margins = beautiful.notification_margin,
   201→--                widget  = wibox.container.margin,
   202→--            },
   203→--            id     = "background_role",
   204→--            widget = naughty.container.background,
   205→--        },
   206→--        strategy = "max",
   207→--        width    = width(beautiful.notification_max_width
   208→--            or beautiful.xresources.apply_dpi(500)),
   209→--        widget   = wibox.container.constraint,
   210→--    }
   211→--
   212→-- @property widget_template
   213→-- @tparam[opt=nil] template|nil widget_template
   214→-- @usebeautiful beautiful.notification_max_width The maximum width for the
   215→--  resulting widget.
   216→
   217→local function generate_widget(args, n)
   218→    local w = gpcall(wibox.widget.base.make_widget_from_value,
   219→        args.widget_template or (n and n.widget_template) or default_widget
   220→    )
   221→
   222→    -- This will happen if the user-provided widget_template is invalid and/or
   223→    -- got unexpected notifications.
   224→    if not w then
   225→        w = gpcall(wibox.widget.base.make_widget_from_value, default_widget)
   226→
   227→        -- In case this happens in an error message itself, make sure the
   228→        -- private error popup code knowns it and can revert to the fallback
   229→        -- popup.
   230→        if not w then
   231→            n._private.widget_template_failed = true
   232→        end
   233→
   234→        return nil
   235→    end
   236→
   237→    if w.set_width then
   238→        w:set_width(n.max_width or beautiful.notification_max_width or dpi(500))
   239→    end
   240→
   241→    -- Call `:set_notification` on all children
   242→    awcommon._set_common_property(w, "notification", n)
   243→
   244→    return w
   245→end
   246→
   247→local function init(self, notification)
   248→    local preset = notification.preset or {}
   249→
   250→    local position = self._private.position or notification.position or
   251→        preset.position or beautiful.notification_position or "top_right"
   252→
   253→    if not self.widget then
   254→        self.widget = generate_widget(self._private, notification)
   255→    end
   256→
   257→    local bg = self._private.widget:get_children_by_id( "background_role" )[1]
   258→
   259→    -- Make sure the border isn't set twice, favor the widget one since it is
   260→    -- shared by the notification list and the notification box.
   261→    if bg then
   262→        if bg.set_notification then
   263→            bg:set_notification(notification)
   264→            self.border_width = 0
   265→        else
   266→            bg:set_bg(notification.bg)
   267→            self.border_width = notification.border_width
   268→        end
   269→    end
   270→
   271→    local s = notification.screen
   272→    assert(s)
   273→
   274→    -- Add the notification to the active list
   275→    assert(init_screen(s)[position], "Invalid position "..position)
   276→
   277→    self:_apply_size_now()
   278→
   279→    table.insert(init_screen(s)[position], self)
   280→
   281→    self._private.update = function() update_position(position, preset) end
   282→    self._private.hide = function(_, value)
   283→        if value then
   284→            finish(self)
   285→        end
   286→    end
   287→
   288→    self:connect_signal("property::geometry", self._private.update)
   289→    notification:weak_connect_signal("property::margin", self._private.update)
   290→    notification:weak_connect_signal("property::suspended", self._private.hide)
   291→    notification:weak_connect_signal("destroyed", self._private.destroy_callback)
   292→
   293→    update_position(position, preset)
   294→
   295→    self.visible = true
   296→end
   297→
   298→function box:set_notification(notif)
   299→    if self._private.notification[1] == notif then return end
   300→
   301→    disconnect(self)
   302→
   303→    init(self, notif)
   304→
   305→    self._private.notification = setmetatable({notif}, {__mode="v"})
   306→
   307→    self:emit_signal("property::notification", notif)
   308→end
   309→
   310→function box:get_notification()
   311→    return self._private.notification[1]
   312→end
   313→
   314→function box:get_position()
   315→    local n = self._private.notification[1]
   316→
   317→    if n then
   318→        return n:get_position()
   319→    end
   320→
   321→    return "top_right"
   322→end
   323→
   324→--- Create a notification popup box.
   325→--
   326→-- @constructorfct naughty.layout.box
   327→-- @tparam[opt=nil] table args
   328→-- @tparam table args.widget_template A widget definition template which will
   329→--  be instantiated for each box.
   330→-- @tparam naughty.notification args.notification The notification object.
   331→-- @tparam string args.position The position. See `naughty.notification.position`.
   332→--@DOC_wibox_constructor_COMMON@
   333→-- @usebeautiful beautiful.notification_position If `position` is not defined
   334→-- in the notification object (or in this constructor).
   335→
   336→local function new(args)
   337→    args = args or {}
   338→
   339→    -- Set the default wibox values
   340→    local new_args = {
   341→        ontop        = true,
   342→        visible      = false,
   343→        bg           = args.bg or beautiful.notification_bg,
   344→        fg           = args.fg or beautiful.notification_fg,
   345→        shape        = args.shape or beautiful.notification_shape,
   346→        border_width = args.border_width or beautiful.notification_border_width or 1,
   347→        border_color = args.border_color or beautiful.notification_border_color,
   348→    }
   349→
   350→    -- The C code needs `pairs` to work, so a full copy is required.
   351→    gtable.crush(new_args, args, true)
   352→
   353→    -- Add a weak-table layer for the screen.
   354→    local weak_args = setmetatable({
   355→        screen = args.notification and args.notification.screen or nil
   356→    }, {__mode="v"})

   148→
   149→    gtable.crush(ret, args)
   150→
   151→    return ret
   152→end

## Somewm Naughty Notification System - Race Condition Analysis Report

I've completed a thorough search of the naughty notification system. Here are the key files and critical race condition vulnerabilities I found:

### KEY FILES STRUCTURE

**Core Notification Files:**
- `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/core.lua` - Global notification management and cleanup logic
- `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/notification.lua` - Individual notification object and timeout handling
- `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/dbus.lua` - DBus interface for notifications
- `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/layout/box.lua` - Notification widget and positioning
- `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/list/notifications.lua` - Notification list widget
- `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/action.lua` - Notification action handling

### CRITICAL RACE CONDITIONS FOUND

#### 1. **SEVERE: Index Corruption During Concurrent Destruction**
**Location:** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/core.lua:247-277`

The `cleanup()` function (line 480-517) has a critical race condition when multiple notifications are destroyed simultaneously:

```lua
local function cleanup(self, reason)
    -- Lines 493-499: Index update loop
    assert(naughty.notifications[scr][self.position][self.idx] == self)
    remove_from_index(self)
    
    -- Update all indices
    for k, n in ipairs(naughty.notifications[scr][self.position]) do
        n.idx = k  -- RACE CONDITION: Between line 494 and here
    end
```

**Race Scenario:** When two notifications N1 and N2 at indices 1 and 2 are destroyed simultaneously:
- N1 calls `remove_from_index()` → removed from list, N2 slides to index 1
- N2 calls `remove_from_index()` → searches for itself by comparing object reference
- If N2's cleanup hasn't run its index update loop yet, `n.idx` may still be 2 (wrong!)
- Then N2's index update loop runs on a partially mutated list
- **Result:** Notifications get lost from `naughty.notifications[scr][position]` or corrupted idx values

**Affected Code:**
```lua
-- core.lua:247-259
local function remove_from_index(n)
    for _, positions in pairs(naughty.notifications) do
        for _, ns in pairs(positions) do
            for k, n2 in ipairs(ns) do
                if n2 == n then
                    assert(ns[k+1] ~= n, "The notification index is corrupted")
                    table.remove(ns, k)
                    return
                end
            end
        end
    end
end
```

---

#### 2. **SEVERE: Timer Callback References Destroyed Notification**
**Location:** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/notification.lua:613-645`

The death timer callback captures `self` in a closure but doesn't check if the notification is destroyed:

```lua
timer_die:connect_signal("timeout", function()
    pcall(die, cst.notification_closed_reason.expired)  -- Line 615
    -- ...
end)
```

The `die` function (line 590-599) is defined as:
```lua
local die = function (reason)
    if reason == cst.notification_closed_reason.expired then
        self.is_expired = true  -- RACE: self might be partially destroyed
        if naughty.expiration_paused then
            table.insert(naughty.notifications._expired[1], self)
            return
        end
    end
    self:destroy(reason)
end
```

**Race Scenario:** 
- User manually destroys notification via `n:destroy()` (sets `is_destroyed = true`)
- Timer fires at same instant
- Timer callback calls `die()` which calls `self:destroy()` again
- First check at line 532 prevents double-destroy, but the destruction signal was already emitted
- This causes **multiple "destroyed" signals** to be emitted with potential side effects

---

#### 3. **CRITICAL: Concurrent Access to `naughty._active` List**
**Location:** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/core.lua:502-507`

The global active notification list is modified without synchronization:

```lua
-- Remove from the global active list.
for k, n in ipairs(naughty._active) do
     if n == self then
        table.remove(naughty._active, k)
        naughty.emit_signal("property::active")  -- Line 505
     end
end
```

**Race Scenario:** If two notifications are destroyed simultaneously and both are in `naughty._active`:
- N1 finds itself at index 1, removes it via `table.remove()`
- N2 starts iteration, expecting to find itself at index 2, but it's now at index 1
- If the signal emission at line 505 triggers code that iterates `naughty._active`, **the list is mutated during iteration**
- **Result:** Notifications get skipped or accessed incorrectly

**Related Signal Emissions:** The `property::active` signal is emitted for each destroyed notification, and listeners might:
- Destroy more notifications (naughty.list.notifications updates, layout recalculation)
- Create new notifications (request handlers)
- Query the active list

---

#### 4. **HIGH: Suspended Notification Cleanup Race**
**Location:** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/core.lua:483-489`

When notifications are suspended, they're moved to `naughty.notifications.suspended`:

```lua
if properties.suspended then
    for k, v in ipairs(naughty.notifications.suspended) do
        if v == self then
            table.remove(naughty.notifications.suspended, k)
            break
        end
    end
end
```

**Race Scenario:** Parallel suspension state changes + notification destruction:
- Notification N1 is suspended (moved to suspended list)
- User toggles `naughty.suspended = false` (calls `resume()`)
- While iterating suspended list in `resume()` (line 305), N1 is destroyed
- The destructor tries to remove N1 from the already-being-iterated list
- **Result:** Iterator state becomes invalid, notifications get skipped

---

#### 5. **HIGH: Timer Closure Captures Stale Data**
**Location:** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/notification.lua:560-565`

The `reset_timeout()` method uses `delayed_call` with a timeout comparison:

```lua
if new_timeout and new_timeout ~= self._private.timeout then
    local previous_timer = self._private.timeout
    timer.delayed_call(function()
        if self._private.timeout == previous_timer then
            self.timeout = new_timeout
        end
    end)
end
```

**Race Scenario:** Multiple rapid property changes:
- Call 1: `reset_timeout(5)` - creates delayed_call with `previous_timer = current_value`
- Call 2: `reset_timeout(10)` - overwrites `self._private.timeout` before delayed_call 1 fires
- When delayed_call 1 fires, the check `if self._private.timeout == previous_timer` fails silently
- Timeout never gets set, or gets set to wrong value
- **Result:** Notification never expires OR expires at wrong time

**Compounded with:** DBus notifications call `reset_timeout()` on every update (line 341 in dbus.lua), triggering this frequently

---

#### 6. **HIGH: Positioning List Weak Reference Corruption**
**Location:** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/layout/box.lua:40-45, 118-136`

The layout uses weak tables for notification positioning:

```lua
by_position[s] = setmetatable({},{__mode = "k"})  -- Weak keys!
-- ...
for _, pos in ipairs { "top_left", ... } do
    by_position[s][pos] = setmetatable({},{__mode = "v"})  -- Weak values!
end
```

In `finish()` (line 118-136):
```lua
for k, v in ipairs(init_screen(self.screen)[self.position]) do
    if v == self then
        table.remove(init_screen(self.screen)[self.position], k)
        break
    end
end
```

**Race Scenario:**
- Notification is being displayed (popup widget holds reference)
- GC runs and the popup widget is marked for collection
- Weak reference to notification is cleared
- `finish()` tries to find the notification by comparing objects
- The comparison `if v == self` might work if `self` is still referenced elsewhere, but the weak table is inconsistent
- **Result:** Notification remains in layout list after GC, causing memory leak or duplicate displays

---

#### 7. **MEDIUM: Signal Cascade During Destruction**
**Location:** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/notification.lua:540`

The destruction signal triggers multiple handlers:

```lua
self:emit_signal("destroyed", reason, keep_visible)
```

Connected handlers in `core.lua:519`:
```lua
naughty.connect_signal("destroyed", cleanup)
```

And in `layout/box.lua:291`:
```lua
notification:weak_connect_signal("destroyed", self._private.destroy_callback)
```

**Race Scenario:** During signal emission:
- User code handler might call `naughty.destroy_all_notifications()`
- This iterates over and destroys all notifications
- While those destructions are firing their own "destroyed" signals
- The original notification's `cleanup()` handler tries to update indices in partially-destroyed lists
- **Result:** Assertion failures or corrupted state (line 493: `assert(naughty.notifications[scr][self.position][self.idx] == self)`)

---

#### 8. **MEDIUM: Expired Notification Storage Race**
**Location:** `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/notification.lua:591-596`

When expiration is paused, notifications are stored in a secondary list:

```lua
if reason == cst.notification_closed_reason.expired then
    self.is_expired = true
    if naughty.expiration_paused then
        table.insert(naughty.notifications._expired[1], self)
        return  -- DOESN'T CALL self:destroy()!
    end
end
```

**Race Scenario:**
- Notification expires while `expiration_paused = true`
- It's added to `_expired[1]` list but NOT destroyed
- User manually calls `n:destroy()`
- Notification is destroyed and removed from `_active`
- Later, `expiration_paused` is set to false
- Code tries to destroy all expired notifications (line 551-553 in core.lua)
- **Result:** Trying to destroy an already-destroyed notification

---

### SUMMARY TABLE OF RACE CONDITIONS

| ID | Severity | Location | Issue | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CRITICAL | `core.lua:493-499` | Index corruption during cleanup | Lost/corrupted notifications |
| 2 | CRITICAL | `notification.lua:615` | Timer references destroyed object | Double-destroy or invalid state |
| 3 | CRITICAL | `core.lua:502-507` | Mutation during list iteration | Skipped notifications, crashes |
| 4 | HIGH | `core.lua:483-489` | Concurrent suspension state change | Iterator invalidation |
| 5 | HIGH | `notification.lua:560-565` | Stale timeout in delayed_call | Wrong expiration time |
| 6 | HIGH | `layout/box.lua:40-45` | Weak reference cleanup | Memory leaks, duplicates |
| 7 | MEDIUM | `notification.lua:540` | Signal cascade recursion | Assertions fail, corruption |
| 8 | MEDIUM | `notification.lua:591-596` | Expired list inconsistency | Double-destroy attempt |

### DEBUG MARKERS IN CODE

The code has helpful debugging markers already in place:

```lua
[NOTIF] set_timeout() called
[NOTIF] set_timeout() after default
[NOTIF] set_timeout() EARLY RETURN
[NOTIF] set_timeout() creating death timer
[NOTIF] Created death timer
[NOTIF] Death timer fired
[NOTIF] die() called
[NOTIF] Death timer stopped
[NOTIF] Starting death timer
[NOTIF] Death timer SUSPENDED
```

These are in `/home/box/git/github/somewm/lua/naughty/notification.lua:585-641` and can help reproduce issues.

### RECOMMENDED REPRODUCTION TEST

To trigger these race conditions, send multiple notifications simultaneously with rapid timeout expiry:

```bash
for i in {1..10}; do notify-send "Test $i" "Message $i" -t 100 & done; wait
```

This should trigger notification #3 (concurrent access to `_active` list) or #1 (index corruption) when multiple notifications expire/are destroyed within milliseconds of each other.

- Notification expires while `expiration_paused = true`

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
--- A notification popup widget.
--
-- By default, the box is composed of many other widgets:
--
--@DOC_wibox_nwidget_default_EXAMPLE@
--
-- @author Emmanuel Lepage Vallee <elv1313@gmail.com>
-- @copyright 2017 Emmanuel Lepage Vallee
-- @popupmod naughty.layout.box
-- @supermodule awful.popup
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

local capi       = {screen=screen}
local beautiful  = require("beautiful")
local gtimer     = require("gears.timer")
local gtable     = require("gears.table")
local wibox      = require("wibox")
local popup      = require("awful.popup")
local awcommon   = require("awful.widget.common")
local placement  = require("awful.placement")
local abutton    = require("awful.button")
local ascreen    = require("awful.screen")
local gpcall     = require("gears.protected_call")
local dpi        = require("beautiful").xresources.apply_dpi
local cst        = require("naughty.constants")

local default_widget = require("naughty.widget._default")

local box, by_position = {}, {}

-- Init the weak tables for each positions. It is done ahead of time rather
-- than when notifications are added to simplify the code.

local function init_screen(s)
    if not s.valid then return end

    if by_position[s] then return by_position[s] end

    by_position[s] = setmetatable({},{__mode = "k"})

    for _, pos in ipairs { "top_left"   , "top_middle"   , "top_right",
                           "bottom_left", "bottom_middle", "bottom_right" } do
        by_position[s][pos] = setmetatable({},{__mode = "v"})
    end

    return by_position[s]
end

local function disconnect(self)
    local n = self._private.notification[1]

    if n then
        n:disconnect_signal("destroyed",
            self._private.destroy_callback)

        n:disconnect_signal("property::margin",
            self._private.update)

        n:disconnect_signal("property::suspended",
            self._private.hide)
    end
end

ascreen.connect_for_each_screen(init_screen)

-- Manually cleanup to help the GC.
capi.screen.connect_signal("removed", function(scr)
    -- By that time, all direct events should have been handled. Cleanup the
    -- leftover. Being a weak table doesn't help Lua 5.1.
    gtimer.delayed_call(function()
        by_position[scr] = nil
    end)
end)

local function get_spacing()
    local margin = beautiful.notification_spacing or dpi(2)
    return {top = margin, bottom = margin}
end

local function get_offset(position, preset)
    preset = preset or {}
    local margin = preset.padding or beautiful.notification_spacing or dpi(4)
    if position:match('_right') then
        return {x = -margin}
    elseif position:match('_left') then
        return {x = margin}
    end
    return {}
end

-- Leverage `awful.placement` to create the stacks.
local function update_position(position, preset)
    local pref  = position:match("top_") and "bottom" or "top"
    local align = position:match("_(.*)")
        :gsub("left", "front"):gsub("right", "back")

    for _, pos in pairs(by_position) do
        for k, wdg in ipairs(pos[position]) do
            local args = {
                geometry            = pos[position][k-1],
                preferred_positions = {pref },
                preferred_anchors   = {align},
                margins             = get_spacing(),
                honor_workarea      = true,
            }
            if k == 1 then
                args.offset = get_offset(position, preset)
            end

            -- The first entry is aligned to the workarea, then the following to the
            -- previous widget.
            placement[k==1 and position:gsub("_middle", "") or "next_to"](wdg, args)
        end
    end
end

local function finish(self)
    self.visible = false
    assert(init_screen(self.screen)[self.position])

    for k, v in ipairs(init_screen(self.screen)[self.position]) do
        if v == self then
            table.remove(init_screen(self.screen)[self.position], k)
            break
        end
    end

    local preset = (self._private.notification[1] or {}).preset

    update_position(self.position, preset)

    disconnect(self)

    self._private.notification = {}
end

-- It isn't a good idea to use the `attach` `awful.placement` property. If the
-- screen is resized or the notification is moved, it causes side effects.
-- Better listen to geometry changes and reflow.
capi.screen.connect_signal("property::geometry", function(s)
    for pos, notifs in pairs(by_position[s]) do
        if #notifs > 0 then
            update_position(pos, notifs[1].preset)
        end
    end
end)

--- The maximum notification width.
-- @beautiful beautiful.notification_max_width
-- @tparam[opt=500] number notification_max_width

--- The maximum notification position.
--
-- Valid values are:
--
-- * top_left
-- * top_middle
-- * top_right
-- * bottom_left
-- * bottom_middle
-- * bottom_right
--
-- @beautiful beautiful.notification_position
-- @tparam[opt="top_right"] string notification_position

--- The widget notification object.
--
-- @property notification
-- @tparam naughty.notification notification
-- @propertydefault This must be provided by the constructor.
-- @propemits true false

--- The widget template to construct the box content.
--
--@DOC_wibox_nwidget_default_EXAMPLE@
--
-- The default template is (less or more):
--
--    {
--        {
--            {
--                {
--                    {
--                        naughty.widget.icon,
--                        {
--                            naughty.widget.title,
--                            naughty.widget.message,
--                            spacing = 4,
--                            layout  = wibox.layout.fixed.vertical,
--                        },
--                        fill_space = true,
--                        spacing    = 4,
--                        layout     = wibox.layout.fixed.horizontal,
--                    },
--                    naughty.list.actions,
--                    spacing = 10,
--                    layout  = wibox.layout.fixed.vertical,
--                },
--                margins = beautiful.notification_margin,
--                widget  = wibox.container.margin,
--            },
--            id     = "background_role",
--            widget = naughty.container.background,
--        },
--        strategy = "max",
--        width    = width(beautiful.notification_max_width
--            or beautiful.xresources.apply_dpi(500)),
--        widget   = wibox.container.constraint,
--    }
--
-- @property widget_template
-- @tparam[opt=nil] template|nil widget_template
-- @usebeautiful beautiful.notification_max_width The maximum width for the
--  resulting widget.

local function generate_widget(args, n)
    local w = gpcall(wibox.widget.base.make_widget_from_value,
        args.widget_template or (n and n.widget_template) or default_widget
    )

    -- This will happen if the user-provided widget_template is invalid and/or
    -- got unexpected notifications.
    if not w then
        w = gpcall(wibox.widget.base.make_widget_from_value, default_widget)

        -- In case this happens in an error message itself, make sure the
        -- private error popup code knowns it and can revert to the fallback
        -- popup.
        if not w then
            n._private.widget_template_failed = true
        end

        return nil
    end

    if w.set_width then
        w:set_width(n.max_width or beautiful.notification_max_width or dpi(500))
    end

    -- Call `:set_notification` on all children
    awcommon._set_common_property(w, "notification", n)

    return w
end

local function init(self, notification)
    local preset = notification.preset or {}

    local position = self._private.position or notification.position or
        preset.position or beautiful.notification_position or "top_right"

    if not self.widget then
        self.widget = generate_widget(self._private, notification)
    end

    local bg = self._private.widget:get_children_by_id( "background_role" )[1]

    -- Make sure the border isn't set twice, favor the widget one since it is
    -- shared by the notification list and the notification box.
    if bg then
        if bg.set_notification then
            bg:set_notification(notification)
            self.border_width = 0
        else
            bg:set_bg(notification.bg)
            self.border_width = notification.border_width
        end
    end

    local s = notification.screen
    assert(s)

    -- Add the notification to the active list
    assert(init_screen(s)[position], "Invalid position "..position)

    self:_apply_size_now()

    table.insert(init_screen(s)[position], self)

    self._private.update = function() update_position(position, preset) end
    self._private.hide = function(_, value)
        if value then
            finish(self)
        end
    end

    self:connect_signal("property::geometry", self._private.update)
    notification:weak_connect_signal("property::margin", self._private.update)
    notification:weak_connect_signal("property::suspended", self._private.hide)
    notification:weak_connect_signal("destroyed", self._private.destroy_callback)

    update_position(position, preset)

    self.visible = true
end

function box:set_notification(notif)
    if self._private.notification[1] == notif then return end

    disconnect(self)

    init(self, notif)

    self._private.notification = setmetatable({notif}, {__mode="v"})

    self:emit_signal("property::notification", notif)
end

function box:get_notification()
    return self._private.notification[1]
end

function box:get_position()
    local n = self._private.notification[1]

    if n then
        return n:get_position()
    end

    return "top_right"
end

--- Create a notification popup box.
--
-- @constructorfct naughty.layout.box
-- @tparam[opt=nil] table args
-- @tparam table args.widget_template A widget definition template which will
--  be instantiated for each box.
-- @tparam naughty.notification args.notification The notification object.
-- @tparam string args.position The position. See `naughty.notification.position`.
--@DOC_wibox_constructor_COMMON@
-- @usebeautiful beautiful.notification_position If `position` is not defined
-- in the notification object (or in this constructor).

local function new(args)
    args = args or {}

    -- Set the default wibox values
    local new_args = {
        ontop        = true,
        visible      = false,
        bg           = args.bg or beautiful.notification_bg,
        fg           = args.fg or beautiful.notification_fg,
        shape        = args.shape or beautiful.notification_shape,
        border_width = args.border_width or beautiful.notification_border_width or 1,
        border_color = args.border_color or beautiful.notification_border_color,
    }

    -- The C code needs `pairs` to work, so a full copy is required.
    gtable.crush(new_args, args, true)

    -- Add a weak-table layer for the screen.
    local weak_args = setmetatable({
        screen = args.notification and args.notification.screen or nil
    }, {__mode="v"})

    setmetatable(new_args, {__index = weak_args})

    -- Generate the box before the popup is created to avoid the size changing
    new_args.widget = generate_widget(new_args, new_args.notification)

    -- It failed, request::fallback will be used, there is nothing left to do.
    if not new_args.widget then return nil end

    local ret = popup(new_args)
    ret._private.notification = {}
    ret._private.widget_template = args.widget_template
    ret._private.position = args.position

    gtable.crush(ret, box, true)

    function ret._private.destroy_callback()
        finish(ret)
    end

    if new_args.notification then
        ret:set_notification(new_args.notification)
    end

    --TODO remove
    local function hide(reason)
        return function ()
            local n = ret._private.notification[1]

            if n then
                n:destroy(reason)
            end
        end
    end

    -- On right click, close the notification without triggering the default action
    ret:buttons(gtable.join(
        abutton({ }, 1, hide(cst.notification_closed_reason.dismissed_by_user)),
        abutton({ }, 3, hide(cst.notification_closed_reason.silent))
    ))

    gtable.crush(ret, box, false)

    return ret
end

return setmetatable(box, {__call = function(_, args) return new(args) end})

Now I see the click handler! Lines 382-396:

```lua
local function hide(reason)
    return function ()
        local n = ret._private.notification[1]
        if n then
            n:destroy(reason)
        end
    end
end

ret:buttons(gtable.join(
    abutton({ }, 1, hide(cst.notification_closed_reason.dismissed_by_user)),
    abutton({ }, 3, hide(cst.notification_closed_reason.silent))
))
```

Left click (button 1) calls `n:destroy(dismissed_by_user)`.


Right click (button 3) calls `n:destroy(silent)`. The notification is stored in a weak table at line 305, so if it gets garbage collected, the click handler would just silently fail since the `if n then` check would be false. But I'm wondering if a notification can actually be garbage collected while it's still visible on screen.

Looking at the reference chain, `naughty._active` should hold strong references to keep notifications alive, so they shouldn't be getting collected prematurely. But the user's 4070S machine is getting stuck notifications that don't dismiss on click, which suggests either the click event isn't reaching the widget at all, the destroy call is failing silently, or something else is preventing the notification from being removed.

The notification uses `awful.popup` which is a drawin surface, so if input focus or pointer events aren't being handled correctly—maybe due to timing issues with surface creation on the NVIDIA driver—the button handlers might never fire. But since clicking works fine in the nested compositor, this points to something specific about the 4070S setup rather than a fundamental code issue.

Let me reconsider what the user originally reported about the stuck notification. The bug hasn't shown up in my tests yet, so I need to focus on what's different about the Firefox/Google Calendar setup on the user's other machine. It could be a specific DBus notification pattern with actions or hints, an NVIDIA-related timing issue, or something screen-output specific. Let me examine how the DBus handler processes Firefox notifications to see what might be triggering this.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- DBUS/Notification support
-- Notify
--
-- @author koniu <gkusnierz@gmail.com>
-- @copyright 2008 koniu
-- @module naughty.dbus
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Package environment
local pairs = pairs
local type = type
local string = string
local capi = { awesome = awesome }
local gsurface = require("gears.surface")
local gdebug  = require("gears.debug")
local protected_call = require("gears.protected_call")
local lgi = require("lgi")
local cairo, Gio, GLib, GObject = lgi.cairo, lgi.Gio, lgi.GLib, lgi.GObject

local schar = string.char
local sbyte = string.byte
local tcat = table.concat
local tins = table.insert
local unpack = unpack or table.unpack -- luacheck: globals unpack (compatibility with Lua 5.1)
local naughty = require("naughty.core")
local cst     = require("naughty.constants")
local nnotif = require("naughty.notification")
local naction = require("naughty.action")

local capabilities = {
    "body", "body-markup", "icon-static", "actions", "action-icons"
}

--- Notification library, dbus bindings
local dbus = { config = {} }

-- This is either nil or a Gio.DBusConnection for emitting signals
local bus_connection

-- DBUS Notification constants
-- https://specifications.freedesktop.org/notification-spec/notification-spec-latest.html#urgency-levels
local urgency = {
    low      = "\0",
    normal   = "\1",
    critical = "\2"
}

--- DBUS notification to preset mapping.
-- The first element is an object containing the filter.
-- If the rules in the filter match, the associated preset will be applied.
-- The rules object can contain the following keys: urgency, category, appname.
-- The second element is the preset.
-- @tfield table 1 low urgency
-- @tfield table 2 normal urgency
-- @tfield table 3 critical urgency
-- @table config.mapping
dbus.config.mapping = cst.config.mapping

local function sendActionInvoked(notificationId, action)
    if bus_connection then
        bus_connection:emit_signal(nil, "/org/freedesktop/Notifications",
        "org.freedesktop.Notifications", "ActionInvoked",
        GLib.Variant("(us)", { notificationId, action }))
    end
end

local function sendNotificationClosed(notificationId, reason)
    if reason <= 0 then
        reason = cst.notification_closed_reason.undefined
    end
    if reason == cst.notification_closed_reason.dismissed_by_user then
        sendActionInvoked(notificationId, "default")
    end
    if bus_connection then
        bus_connection:emit_signal(nil, "/org/freedesktop/Notifications",
        "org.freedesktop.Notifications", "NotificationClosed",
        GLib.Variant("(uu)", { notificationId, reason }))
    end
end

local function convert_icon(w, h, rowstride, channels, data)
    -- Do the arguments look sane? (e.g. we have enough data)
    local expected_length = rowstride * (h - 1) + w * channels
    if w < 0 or h < 0 or rowstride < 0 or (channels ~= 3 and channels ~= 4) or
        string.len(data) < expected_length then
        w = 0
        h = 0
    end

    local format = cairo.Format[channels == 4 and 'ARGB32' or 'RGB24']

    -- Figure out some stride magic (cairo dictates rowstride)
    local stride = cairo.Format.stride_for_width(format, w)
    local append = schar(0):rep(stride - 4 * w)
    local offset = 0

    -- Now convert each row on its own
    local rows = {}

    for _ = 1, h do
        local this_row = {}

        for i = 1 + offset, w * channels + offset, channels do
            local R, G, B, A = sbyte(data, i, i + channels - 1)
            tins(this_row, schar(B, G, R, A or 255))
        end

        -- Handle rowstride, offset is stride for the input, append for output
        tins(this_row, append)
        tins(rows, tcat(this_row))

        offset = offset + rowstride
    end

    local pixels = tcat(rows)
    local surf = cairo.ImageSurface.create_for_data(pixels, format, w, h, stride)

    -- The surface refers to 'pixels', which can be freed by the GC. Thus,
    -- duplicate the surface to create a copy of the data owned by cairo.
    local res = gsurface.duplicate_surface(surf)
    surf:finish()
    return res
end

                local b = string.char(hints.urgency)
                if key == b then
                    args.urgency = name
                end
            end
        end

        args.urgency = args.urgency or "normal"

        -- Try to update existing objects when possible
        notification = naughty.get_by_id(replaces_id)

        if notification then
            if not notification._private._unique_sender then
                -- If this happens, the notification is either trying to
                -- highjack content created within AwesomeWM or it is garbage
                -- to begin with.
                gdebug.print_warning(
                    "A notification has been received, but tried to update "..
                    "the content of a notification it does not own."
                )
            elseif notification._private._unique_sender ~= sender then
                -- Nothing says you cannot and some scripts may do it
                -- accidentally, but this is rather unexpected.
                gdebug.print_warning(
                    "Notification "..notification.title.." is being updated"..
                    "by a different DBus connection ("..sender.."), this is "..
                    "suspicious. The original connection was "..
                    notification._private._unique_sender
                )
            end

            for k, v in pairs(args) do
                if k == "destroy" then k = "destroy_cb" end
                notification[k] = v
            end

            -- Update the icon if necessary.
            if app_icon ~= notification._private.app_icon then
                notification._private.app_icon = app_icon

                naughty._emit_signal_if(
                    "request::icon", function()
                        if notification._private.icon then return true end
                    end, notification, "dbus_clear", {}
                )
            end

            -- Even if no property changed, restart the timeout.
            notification:reset_timeout()
        else
            -- Only set the sender for new notifications.
            args._unique_sender = sender

            notification = nnotif(args)

            notification:connect_signal("destroyed", function(_, r) args.destroy(r) end)
        end

        invocation:return_value(GLib.Variant("(u)", { notification.id }))
        return
    end

    invocation:return_value(GLib.Variant("(u)", { nnotif._gen_next_id() }))
end

OK, so when notifications have their own individual timers that fire at slightly different times, they all get cleaned up properly because each `destroy()` happens in its own timer callback. The bug only manifests when multiple notifications are destroyed in the SAME Lua call (same event loop tick), which causes the `ipairs` + `table.remove` issue.

So the scenario is:
1. Two persistent notifications (`timeout=0`) arrive
2. Something tries to destroy them both in the same Lua execution (not individual timer callbacks)
3. `ipairs` + `table.remove` causes the last one to be skipped

When does this happen in practice?


- User code iterating through active notifications and destroying them all at once
- A signal handler that cascades destruction
- When `naughty.suspended` is toggled, expired notifications might be batch-destroyed

The user's case with Firefox and Google Calendar involves persistent notifications that require manual closing. The real issue seems to be that when multiple calendar events arrive simultaneously, something in the notification handling is triggering batch destruction in the same Lua execution, leaving the last notification stuck.

Looking at how timers work in the event loop — if multiple notifications have short timeouts and their expiration callbacks fire in the same iteration, the first callback's cleanup might modify the active notifications table while the second callback is still running, causing index corruption.

Examining the core notification loop... about a different scenario. What if the issue is in `naughty.notifications[screen][position]`? When a notification is destroyed, it updates the indices of all remaining notifications in that position list, so if two notifications are destroyed in sequence, the second one's `self.idx` might be pointing to the wrong location after the first one reindexes everything. But looking closer, `remove_from_index` actually searches by object reference rather than relying on `self.idx`, so that shouldn't be the problem either.

Let me step back and focus on what I can actually reproduce. The `ipairs` plus `table.remove` pattern is definitely buggy, and emitting `property::active` signals during cleanup could trigger cascading issues. For the user's specific case though, I'm thinking the most likely culprit is that Google Calendar notifications arrive via DBus, possibly with actions attached, and something goes wrong when the user interacts with them.

Actually, I wonder if Firefox is sending replacement notifications when it reacts to the `ActionInvoked` signal for dismissed notifications—that could create a problematic loop.
