})

-- @DOC_CLIENT_BUTTONS@
client.connect_signal("request::default_mousebindings", function()
    awful.mouse.append_client_mousebindings({
        awful.button({ }, 1, function (c)
            c:activate { context = "mouse_click" }
        end),
        awful.button({ modkey }, 1, function (c)
            c:activate { context = "mouse_click", action = "mouse_move"  }
        end),
        awful.button({ modkey }, 3, function (c)
            c:activate { context = "mouse_click", action = "mouse_resize"}
        end),
    })
end)

-- @DOC_CLIENT_KEYBINDINGS@
client.connect_signal("request::default_keybindings", function()
    awful.keyboard.append_client_keybindings({
        awful.key({ modkey,           }, "f",
            function (c)
                c.fullscreen = not c.fullscreen
                c:raise()
            end,
            {description = "toggle fullscreen", group = "client"}),
        awful.key({ modkey, "Shift"   }, "c",      function (c) c:kill()                         end,
                {description = "close", group = "client"}),
        awful.key({ modkey, "Control" }, "space",  awful.client.floating.toggle                     ,
                {description = "toggle floating", group = "client"}),
        awful.key({ modkey, "Control" }, "Return", function (c) c:swap(awful.client.getmaster()) end,
                {description = "move to master", group = "client"}),
        awful.key({ modkey,           }, "o",      function (c) c:move_to_screen()               end,
                {description = "move to screen", group = "client"}),
        awful.key({ modkey, "Control" }, "t",      function (c) c.ontop = not c.ontop            end,
                {description = "toggle keep on top", group = "client"}),
        -- show/hide titlebar
        awful.key({ modkey }, "t", awful.titlebar.toggle,
                { description = "Show/Hide Titlebars", group = "client" }),                
        awful.key({ modkey,           }, "n",
            function (c)
                -- The client currently has the input focus, so it cannot be
                -- minimized, since minimized clients can't have the focus.
                c.minimized = true
            end ,
            {description = "minimize", group = "client"}),
        awful.key({ modkey,           }, "m",
            function (c)
                c.maximized = not c.maximized
                c:raise()
            end ,
            {description = "(un)maximize", group = "client"}),
        awful.key({ modkey, "Control" }, "m",
            function (c)
                c.maximized_vertical = not c.maximized_vertical
                c:raise()
            end ,
            {description = "(un)maximize vertically", group = "client"}),
        awful.key({ modkey, "Shift"   }, "m",
            function (c)
                c.maximized_horizontal = not c.maximized_horizontal
                c:raise()
            end ,
            {description = "(un)maximize horizontally", group = "client"}),
    })
end)

-- Steam bug with window outside of the screen
client.connect_signal("property::position", function(c)
    if c.class == 'Steam' then
        local g = c.screen.geometry
        if c.y + c.height > g.height then
            c.y = g.height - c.height
            naughty.notify {
                text = "restricted window: " .. c.name,
            }
        end
        if c.x + c.width > g.width then
            c.x = g.width - c.width
        end
    end
end)

-- }}}

-- {{{ Rules
-- Rules to apply to new clients.
ruled.client.connect_signal("request::rules", function()
    -- All clients will match this rule.
    ruled.client.append_rule {
        id         = "global",
        rule       = {},
        properties = {
            focus     = awful.client.focus.filter,
            raise     = true,
            screen    = awful.screen.preferred,
            placement = awful.placement.no_overlap + awful.placement.no_offscreen
        }
    }

    -- Add titlebars to normal clients and dialogs
    ruled.client.append_rule {
        id         = "dialogs",
        rule_any   = { type = { "dialog" } },
        except_any = {
            -- place here exceptions for special dialogs windows
        },
        properties = { floating = true },
        callback   = function(c)
            awful.placement.centered(c, nil)
        end
    }

    -- All Dialogs are floating and center
    ruled.client.append_rule {
        id         = "titlebars",
        rule_any   = { type = { "normal", "dialog" } },
        properties = { titlebars_enabled = true }
    }

    ruled.client.append_rule {
        id         = "floating",
        rule_any   = {
            name = { "Ulauncher - Application Launcher" },
        },
        properties = {
            focus        = awful.client.focus.filter,
            raise        = true,
            screen       = awful.screen.preferred,
            border_width = 0,
        }
    }

    -- Floating clients.
    ruled.client.append_rule {
        id         = "floating",
        rule_any   = {
            instance = { "copyq", "pinentry" },
            class    = {
                "Arandr", "Blueman-manager", "Gpick", "Kruler", "Sxiv",
                "Tor Browser", "Wpa_gui", "veromix", "xtightvncviewer",
                "Pamac-manager",
                "Polkit-gnome-authentication-agent-1",
                "Polkit-kde-authentication-agent-1",
                "Gcr-prompter",
            },
            -- Note that the name property shown in xprop might be set slightly after creation of the client
            -- and the name shown there might not match defined rules here.
            name     = {
                "Event Tester", -- xev.
                "Remmina Remote Desktop Client",
                "win0",
            },
            role     = {
                "AlarmWindow",   -- Thunderbird's calendar.
                "ConfigManager", -- Thunderbird's about:config.
                "pop-up",        -- e.g. Google Chrome's (detached) Developer Tools.
            }
        },
        properties = { floating = true },
        callback   = function(c)
            awful.placement.centered(c, nil)
        end
    }

    -- FullHD Resolution for Specific Apps
    ruled.client.append_rule {
        id         = "dialogs",
        rule_any   = {
            instance = { "remmina", }
        },
        except_any = {
            name = {
                "Remmina Remote Desktop Client"
            }
        },
        properties = { floating = true },
        callback   = function(c)
            c.width = 1980
            c.height = 1080
            awful.placement.centered(c, nil)
        end
    }

    -- Set Blender to always map on the tag 4 in screen 1.
    ruled.client.append_rule {
        rule_any   = {
            name = { "Blender" }
        },
        properties = {
            tag = screen[1].tags[4],
        },
    }

    -- Set Obsidian to always map on the tag 2 in screen 1.
    ruled.client.append_rule {
        rule_any   = {
            name = { "Obsidian" }
        },
        properties = {
            tag = screen[1].tags[2],
        },
    }

    ruled.client.append_rule {
        rule_any = {
            name = { "GLava" }
        },
        properties = {
            focusable = false,
            ontop = true,
            skip_taskbar = true
        },
        callback = function(c)
            local img = cairo.ImageSurface(cairo.Format.A1, 0, 0)
            c.shape_input = img._native
            img.finish()
        end
    }
end)

-- }}}

client.connect_signal("manage", function(c)
    -- Similar behaviour as other window managers DWM, XMonad.
    -- Master-Slave layout new client goes to the slave, master is kept
    -- If you need new slave as master press: ctrl + super + return
    if not awesome.startup then c:to_secondary_section() end
end)

-- {{{ Titlebars
-- @DOC_TITLEBARS@
-- Add a titlebar if titlebars_enabled is set to true in the rules.
client.connect_signal("request::titlebars", function(c)
    -- buttons for the titlebar
    local buttons = {
        awful.button({ }, 1, function()
            c:activate { context = "titlebar", action = "mouse_move"  }
        end),
        awful.button({ }, 3, function()
            c:activate { context = "titlebar", action = "mouse_resize"}
        end),
    }

    awful.titlebar(c).widget = {
        { -- Left
            awful.titlebar.widget.iconwidget(c),
            buttons = buttons,
            layout  = wibox.layout.fixed.horizontal
        },
        { -- Middle
            { -- Title
                halign = "center",
                widget = awful.titlebar.widget.titlewidget(c)
            },
            buttons = buttons,
            layout  = wibox.layout.flex.horizontal
        },
        { -- Right
            awful.titlebar.widget.floatingbutton (c),
            awful.titlebar.widget.maximizedbutton(c),
            awful.titlebar.widget.stickybutton   (c),
            awful.titlebar.widget.ontopbutton    (c),
            awful.titlebar.widget.closebutton    (c),
            layout = wibox.layout.fixed.horizontal()
        },
        layout = wibox.layout.align.horizontal
    }
    awful.titlebar.hide(c)
end)
-- }}}

-- {{{ Notifications

ruled.notification.connect_signal('request::rules', function()
    -- All notifications will match this rule.
    ruled.notification.append_rule {
        rule       = { },
        properties = {
            screen           = awful.screen.preferred,
            implicit_timeout = 5,
        }
    }
end)

naughty.connect_signal("request::display", function(n)
    naughty.layout.box { notification = n }
end)

-- }}}

-- Enable sloppy focus, so that focus follows mouse.
client.connect_signal("mouse::enter", function(c)
    c:activate { context = "mouse_enter", raise = false }
end)

--- Allows to use the wibox widget system to draw the wallpaper.
--
-- Rather than simply having a function to set an image
-- (stretched, centered or tiled) like most wallpaper tools, this module
-- leverage the full widget system to draw the wallpaper. Note that the result
-- is **not** interactive. If you want an interactive wallpaper, better use
-- a `wibox` object with the `below` property set to `true` and maximized
-- using `awful.placement.maximized`.
--
-- It is possible to create an `awful.wallpaper` object from any places, but
-- it is recommanded to do it from the `request::wallpaper` signal handler.
-- That signal is called everytime something which could affect the wallpaper
-- rendering changes, such as new screens.
--
-- Single image
-- ============
--
-- This is the default `rc.lua` wallpaper format. It fills the whole screen
-- and stretches the image while keeping the aspect ratio.
--

-- If the image aspect ratio doesn't match, the `bg` property can be used to
-- fill the empty area:

--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_mazimized2_EXAMPLE@
--
-- It is also possible to stretch the image:
--
--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_mazimized3_EXAMPLE@

-- To maintain the image's aspect ratio while filling the
-- screen, the image can be cropped using `gears.surface`:
--

-- Finally, it is also possible to use simpler "branding" in a corner using
-- `awful.placement`:
--

-- Tiled

-- This one tiles a shape using the `wibox.widget.separator` widget:

--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_tiled2_EXAMPLE@
--
-- See the `wibox.container.tile` for more advanced tiling configuration
-- options.
--
-- Solid colors and gradients
-- ==========================
--
-- Solid colors can be set using the `bg` property mentionned above. It
-- is also possible to set gradients:
--

1→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→-- Functions for setting the wallpaper.
     3→--
     4→-- This module is deprecated, please use `awful.wallpaper`.
     5→--
     6→-- @author Uli Schlachter
     7→-- @copyright 2012 Uli Schlachter
     8→-- @utillib gears.wallpaper
     9→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    10→
    11→local cairo = require("lgi").cairo
    12→local color = require("gears.color")
    13→local surface = require("gears.surface")
    14→local timer = require("gears.timer")
    15→local debug = require("gears.debug")
    16→local root = root
    17→
    18→local wallpaper = { mt = {} }
    19→
    20→local function root_geometry()
    21→    local width, height = root.size()
    22→    return { x = 0, y = 0, width = width, height = height }
    23→end
    24→
    25→-- Information about a pending wallpaper change, see prepare_context()
    26→local pending_wallpaper = nil
    27→
    28→local function get_screen(s)
    29→    return s and screen[s]
    30→end
    31→
    32→--- Prepare the needed state for setting a wallpaper.
    33→-- This function returns a cairo context through which a wallpaper can be drawn.
    34→-- The context is only valid for a short time and should not be saved in a
    35→-- global variable.
    36→-- @param s The screen to set the wallpaper on or nil for all screens
    37→-- @return[1] The available geometry (table with entries width and height)
    38→-- @return[1] A cairo context that the wallpaper should be drawn to.
    39→-- @deprecated gears.wallpaper.prepare_context
    40→function wallpaper.prepare_context(s)
    41→    debug.deprecate("Use `awful.wallpaper`", {deprecated_in=5})
    42→
    43→    s = get_screen(s)
    44→
    45→    local root_width, root_height = root.size()
    46→    local geom = s and s.geometry or root_geometry()
    47→    local source, target, cr
    48→
    49→    if not pending_wallpaper then
    50→        -- Prepare a pending wallpaper
    51→        source = surface(root.wallpaper())
    52→        target = source:create_similar(cairo.Content.COLOR, root_width, root_height)
    53→
    54→        -- Set the wallpaper (delayed)
    55→        timer.delayed_call(function()
    56→            local paper = pending_wallpaper
    57→            pending_wallpaper = nil
    58→            wallpaper.set(paper.surface)
    59→            paper.surface:finish()
    60→        end)
    61→    elseif root_width > pending_wallpaper.width or root_height > pending_wallpaper.height then
    62→        -- The root window was resized while a wallpaper is pending
    63→        source = pending_wallpaper.surface
    64→        target = source:create_similar(cairo.Content.COLOR, root_width, root_height)
    65→    else
    66→        -- Draw to the already-pending wallpaper
    67→        source = nil
    68→        target = pending_wallpaper.surface
    69→    end
    70→
    71→    cr = cairo.Context(target)
    72→
    73→    if source then
    74→        -- Copy the old wallpaper to the new one
    75→        cr:save()
    76→        cr.operator = cairo.Operator.SOURCE
    77→        cr:set_source_surface(source, 0, 0)
    78→        cr:paint()
    79→        cr:restore()
    80→    end
    81→
    82→    pending_wallpaper = {
    83→        surface = target,
    84→        width = root_width,
    85→        height = root_height
    86→    }
    87→
    88→    -- Only draw to the selected area
    89→    cr:translate(geom.x, geom.y)
    90→    cr:rectangle(0, 0, geom.width, geom.height)
    91→    cr:clip()
    92→
    93→    return geom, cr
    94→end
    95→
    96→--- Set the current wallpaper.
    97→-- @param pattern The wallpaper that should be set. This can be a cairo surface,
    98→--   a description for gears.color or a cairo pattern.
    99→-- @see gears.color
   100→-- @deprecated gears.wallpaper.set
   101→function wallpaper.set(pattern)
   102→    debug.deprecate("Use `awful.wallpaper`", {deprecated_in=5})
   103→
   104→    if cairo.Surface:is_type_of(pattern) then
   105→        pattern = cairo.Pattern.create_for_surface(pattern)
   106→    end
   107→    if type(pattern) == "string" or type(pattern) == "table" then
   108→        pattern = color(pattern)
   109→    end
   110→    if not cairo.Pattern:is_type_of(pattern) then
   111→        error("wallpaper.set() called with an invalid argument")
   112→    end
   113→    root.wallpaper(pattern)
   114→end
   115→
   116→--- Set a centered wallpaper.
   117→-- @param surf The wallpaper to center. Either a cairo surface or a file name.
   118→-- @param s The screen whose wallpaper should be set. Can be nil, in which case
   119→--   all screens are set.
   120→-- @param background The background color that should be used. Gets handled via
   121→--   gears.color. The default is black.
   122→-- @param scale The scale factor for the wallpaper. Default is 1 (original size).
   123→-- @see gears.color
   124→-- @deprecated gears.wallpaper.centered
   125→function wallpaper.centered(surf, s, background, scale)
   126→    debug.deprecate("Use `awful.wallpaper`", {deprecated_in=5})
   127→
   128→    local geom, cr = wallpaper.prepare_context(s)
   129→    local original_surf = surf
   130→    surf = surface.load_uncached(surf)
   131→    background = color(background)
   132→
   133→    -- Set default scale if unset
   134→    if not scale or scale <= 0 then
   135→        scale = 1
   136→    end
   137→
   138→    -- Fill the area with the background
   139→    cr.operator = cairo.Operator.SOURCE
   140→    cr.source = background
   141→    cr:paint()
   142→
   143→    -- Now center the surface
   144→    local w, h = surface.get_size(surf)
   145→    cr:translate((geom.width - (w * scale)) / 2, (geom.height - (h * scale)) / 2)
   146→    cr:rectangle(0, 0, (w * scale), (h * scale))
   147→
   148→    cr:clip()
   149→    cr:scale(scale, scale)
   150→
   151→    cr:set_source_surface(surf, 0, 0)
   152→    cr:paint()
   153→    if surf ~= original_surf then
   154→        surf:finish()
   155→    end
   156→    if cr.status ~= "SUCCESS" then
   157→        debug.print_warning("Cairo context entered error state: " .. cr.status)
   158→    end
   159→end
   160→
   161→--- Set a tiled wallpaper.
   162→-- @param surf The wallpaper to tile. Either a cairo surface or a file name.
   163→-- @param s The screen whose wallpaper should be set. Can be nil, in which case
   164→--   all screens are set.
   165→-- @param offset This can be set to a table with entries x and y.
   166→-- @deprecated gears.wallpaper.tiled
   167→function wallpaper.tiled(surf, s, offset)
   168→    debug.deprecate("Use `awful.wallpaper`", {deprecated_in=5})
   169→
   170→    local _, cr = wallpaper.prepare_context(s)
   171→
   172→    if offset then
   173→        cr:translate(offset.x, offset.y)
   174→    end
   175→
   176→    local original_surf = surf
   177→    surf = surface.load_uncached(surf)
   178→    local pattern = cairo.Pattern.create_for_surface(surf)
   179→    pattern.extend = cairo.Extend.REPEAT
   180→    cr.source = pattern
   181→    cr.operator = cairo.Operator.SOURCE
   182→    cr:paint()
   183→    if surf ~= original_surf then
   184→        surf:finish()
   185→    end
   186→    if cr.status ~= "SUCCESS" then
   187→        debug.print_warning("Cairo context entered error state: " .. cr.status)
   188→    end
   189→end
   190→
   191→--- Set a maximized wallpaper.
   192→-- @param surf The wallpaper to set. Either a cairo surface or a file name.
   193→-- @param s The screen whose wallpaper should be set. Can be nil, in which case
   194→--   all screens are set.
   195→-- @param ignore_aspect If this is true, the image's aspect ratio is ignored.
   196→--   The default is to honor the aspect ratio.
   197→-- @param offset This can be set to a table with entries x and y.
   198→-- @deprecated gears.wallpaper.maximized
   199→function wallpaper.maximized(surf, s, ignore_aspect, offset)
   200→    debug.deprecate("Use `awful.wallpaper`", {deprecated_in=5})
   201→
   202→    local geom, cr = wallpaper.prepare_context(s)
   203→    local original_surf = surf
   204→    surf = surface.load_uncached(surf)
   205→    local w, h = surface.get_size(surf)
   206→    local aspect_w = geom.width / w
   207→    local aspect_h = geom.height / h
   208→
   209→    if not ignore_aspect then
   210→        aspect_h = math.max(aspect_w, aspect_h)
   211→        aspect_w = math.max(aspect_w, aspect_h)
   212→    end
   213→    cr:scale(aspect_w, aspect_h)
   214→
   215→    if offset then
   216→        cr:translate(offset.x, offset.y)
   217→    elseif not ignore_aspect then
   218→        local scaled_width = geom.width / aspect_w
   219→        local scaled_height = geom.height / aspect_h
   220→        cr:translate((scaled_width - w) / 2, (scaled_height - h) / 2)
   221→    end
   222→
   223→    cr:set_source_surface(surf, 0, 0)
   224→    cr.operator = cairo.Operator.SOURCE
   225→    cr:paint()
   226→    if surf ~= original_surf then
   227→        surf:finish()
   228→    end
   229→    if cr.status ~= "SUCCESS" then
   230→        debug.print_warning("Cairo context entered error state: " .. cr.status)
   231→    end
   232→end
   233→
   234→--- Set a fitting wallpaper.
   235→-- @param surf The wallpaper to set. Either a cairo surface or a file name.
   236→-- @param s The screen whose wallpaper should be set. Can be nil, in which case
   237→--   all screens are set.
   238→-- @param background The background color that should be used. Gets handled via
   239→--   gears.color. The default is black.
   240→-- @see gears.color
   241→-- @deprecated gears.wallpaper.fit
   242→function wallpaper.fit(surf, s, background)
   243→    debug.deprecate("Use `awful.wallpaper`", {deprecated_in=5})
   244→
   245→    local geom, cr = wallpaper.prepare_context(s)
   246→    local original_surf = surf
   247→    surf = surface.load_uncached(surf)
   248→    background = color(background)
   249→
   250→    -- Fill the area with the background
   251→    cr.operator = cairo.Operator.SOURCE
   252→    cr.source = background
   253→    cr:paint()
   254→
   255→    -- Now fit the surface
   256→    local w, h = surface.get_size(surf)
   257→    local scale = geom.width / w
   258→    if h * scale > geom.height then
   259→       scale = geom.height / h
   260→    end
   261→    cr:translate((geom.width - (w * scale)) / 2, (geom.height - (h * scale)) / 2)
   262→    cr:rectangle(0, 0, w * scale, h * scale)
   263→    cr:clip()
   264→    cr:scale(scale, scale)
   265→    cr:set_source_surface(surf, 0, 0)
   266→    cr:paint()
   267→    if surf ~= original_surf then
   268→        surf:finish()
   269→    end
   270→    if cr.status ~= "SUCCESS" then
   271→        debug.print_warning("Cairo context entered error state: " .. cr.status)
   272→    end
   273→end
   274→
   275→return wallpaper
   276→

1→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
     2→--- Allows to use the wibox widget system to draw the wallpaper.
     3→--
     4→-- Rather than simply having a function to set an image
     5→-- (stretched, centered or tiled) like most wallpaper tools, this module
     6→-- leverage the full widget system to draw the wallpaper. Note that the result
     7→-- is **not** interactive. If you want an interactive wallpaper, better use
     8→-- a `wibox` object with the `below` property set to `true` and maximized
     9→-- using `awful.placement.maximized`.
    10→--
    11→-- It is possible to create an `awful.wallpaper` object from any places, but
    12→-- it is recommanded to do it from the `request::wallpaper` signal handler.
    13→-- That signal is called everytime something which could affect the wallpaper
    14→-- rendering changes, such as new screens.
    15→--
    16→-- Single image
    17→-- ============
    18→--
    19→-- This is the default `rc.lua` wallpaper format. It fills the whole screen
    20→-- and stretches the image while keeping the aspect ratio.
    21→--
    22→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_mazimized1_EXAMPLE@

    24→-- If the image aspect ratio doesn't match, the `bg` property can be used to

    34→-- screen, the image can be cropped using `gears.surface`:
    35→--
    36→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_mazimized4_EXAMPLE@
    37→--
    38→-- Finally, it is also possible to use simpler "branding" in a corner using
    39→-- `awful.placement`:
    40→--
    41→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_corner1_EXAMPLE@
    42→--
    43→-- Tiled
    44→-- =====
    45→--
    46→-- This example tiles an image:
    47→--
    48→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_tiled1_EXAMPLE@
    49→--
    50→-- This one tiles a shape using the `wibox.widget.separator` widget:

    55→-- options.
    56→--
    57→-- Solid colors and gradients
    58→-- ==========================
    59→--
    60→-- Solid colors can be set using the `bg` property mentionned above. It
    61→-- is also possible to set gradients:
    62→--
    63→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_gradient1_EXAMPLE@
    64→--
    65→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_gradient2_EXAMPLE@
    66→--
    67→-- Widgets
    68→-- =======
    69→--
    70→-- It is possible to create a wallpaper using any widgets. However, keep
    71→-- in mind that the wallpaper surface is not interactive, so some widgets
    72→-- like the sliders will render, but will not behave correctly. Also, it
    73→    -- is not recommanded to update the wallpaper too often. This is very slow.
    74→--
    75→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_widget2_EXAMPLE@
    76→--
    77→-- Cairo graphics API
    78→-- ==================
    79→--
    80→-- AwesomeWM widgets are backed by Cairo. So it is always possible to get
    81→-- access to the Cairo context directly to do some vector art:
    82→--
    83→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_widget1_EXAMPLE@
    84→--
    85→--
    86→-- SVG vector images
    87→-- =================
    88→--
    89→-- SVG are supported if `librsvg` is installed. Please note that `librsvg`
    90→-- doesn't implement all filters you might find in the latest version of
    91→-- your web browser. It is possible some advanced SVG will not look exactly
    92→-- as they do in a web browser or even Inkscape. However, for most images,
    93→-- it should look identical.
    94→--
    95→-- Our SVG support goes beyond simple rendering. It is possible to set a
    96→-- custom CSS stylesheet (see `wibox.widget.imagebox.stylesheet`):
    97→--
    98→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_svg_EXAMPLE@
    99→--
   100→-- Note that in the example above, it is raw SVG code, but it is also possible
   101→-- to use a file path. If you have a `.svgz`, you need to uncompress it first
   102→-- using `gunzip` or a software like Inkscape.
   103→--
   104→-- Multiple screen
   105→-- ===============
   106→--
   107→-- The default `rc.lua` creates a new wallpaper everytime `request::wallpaper`
   108→-- is emitted. This is well suited for having a single wallpaper per screen.
   109→-- It is also much simpler to implement slideshows and add/remove screens.
   110→--
   111→-- However, it isn't wall suited for wallpaper rendered across multiple screens.
   112→-- For this case, it is better to capture the return value of `awful.wallpaper {}`
   113→-- as a global variable. Then manually call `add_screen` and `remove_screen` when
   114→-- needed. A shortcut can be to do:
   115→--
   116→-- @DOC_text_awful_wallpaper_multi_screen_EXAMPLE@
   117→--
   118→-- Slideshow
   119→-- =========
   120→--
   121→-- Slideshows (changing the wallpaper after a few minutes) can be implemented
   122→-- directly using a timer and callback, but it is more elegant to simply request
   123→-- a new wallpaper, then get a random image from within the request handler. This
   124→-- way, corner cases such as adding and removing screens are handled:
   125→--
   126→--@DOC_awful_wallpaper_slideshow1_EXAMPLE@
   127→--
   128→-- @author Emmanuel Lepage Vallee <elv1313@gmail.com>
   129→-- @copyright 2019 Emmanuel Lepage Vallee
   130→-- @popupmod awful.wallpaper
   131→---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   132→require("awful._compat")
   133→local gtable     = require( "gears.table"               )
   134→local gobject    = require( "gears.object"              )
   135→local gcolor     = require( "gears.color"               )
   136→local gtimer     = require( "gears.timer"               )
   137→local surface    = require( "gears.surface"             )
   138→local base       = require( "wibox.widget.base"         )
   139→local background = require( "wibox.container.background")
   140→local beautiful  = require( "beautiful"                 )
   141→local cairo      = require( "lgi" ).cairo
   142→local draw       = require( "wibox.widget" ).draw_to_cairo_context
   143→local grect      = require( "gears.geometry" ).rectangle
   144→
   145→local capi = { screen = screen, root = root }
   146→
   147→local module = {}
   148→
   149→local function get_screen(s)
   150→    return s and capi.screen[s]
   151→end
   152→
   153→-- Screen as key, wallpaper as values.
   154→local pending_repaint = setmetatable({}, {__mode = 'k'})
   155→
   156→local backgrounds = setmetatable({}, {__mode = 'k'})
   157→
   158→local panning_modes = {}
   159→
   160→-- Get a list of all screen areas.
   161→local function get_rectangles(screens, honor_workarea, honor_padding)
   162→    local ret = {}
   163→
   164→    for _, s in ipairs(screens) do
   165→        table.insert(ret, s:get_bounding_geometry {
   166→            honor_padding  = honor_padding,
   167→            honor_workarea = honor_workarea
   168→        })
   169→    end
   170→
   171→    return ret
   172→end
   173→
   174→-- Outer perimeter of all rectangles.
   175→function panning_modes.outer(self)
   176→    local rectangles = get_rectangles(self.screens, self.honor_workarea, self.honor_padding)
   177→    local p1, p2 = {x = math.huge, y = math.huge}, {x = 0, y = 0}
   178→
   179→    for _, rect in ipairs(rectangles) do
   180→        p1.x, p1.y = math.min(p1.x, rect.x),  math.min(p1.y, rect.y)
   181→        p2.x, p2.y = math.max(p2.x, rect.x +  rect.width),  math.max(p2.y, rect.y + rect.height)
   182→    end
   183→
   184→    -- Never try to paint this, it would freeze the system.
   185→    assert(p1.x ~= math.huge and p1.y ~= math.huge, "Setting wallpaper failed"..#self.screens)
   186→
   187→    return {
   188→        x      = p1.x,
   189→        y      = p1.y,
   190→        width  = p2.x - p1.x,
   191→        height = p2.y - p1.y,
   192→    }
   193→end
   194→
   195→-- Horizontal inner perimeter of all rectangles.
   196→function panning_modes.inner_horizontal(self)
   197→    local rectangles = get_rectangles(self.screens, self.honor_workarea, self.honor_padding)
   198→    local p1, p2 = {x = math.huge, y = 0}, {x = 0, y = math.huge}
   199→
   200→    for _, rect in ipairs(rectangles) do
   201→        p1.x, p1.y = math.min(p1.x, rect.x),  math.max(p1.y, rect.y)
   202→        p2.x, p2.y = math.max(p2.x, rect.x +  rect.width),  math.min(p2.y, rect.y + rect.height)
   203→    end
   204→
   205→    -- Never try to paint this, it would freeze the system.
   206→    assert(p1.x ~= math.huge and p2.y ~= math.huge, "Setting wallpaper failed")
   207→
   208→    return {
   209→        x      = p1.x,
   210→        y      = p1.y,
   211→        width  = p2.x - p1.x,
   212→        height = p2.y - p1.y,
   213→    }
   214→end
   215→
   216→-- Vertical inner perimeter of all rectangles.
   217→function panning_modes.inner_vertical(self)
   218→    local rectangles = get_rectangles(self.screens, self.honor_workarea, self.honor_padding)
   219→    local p1, p2 = {x = 0, y = math.huge}, {x = math.huge, y = 0}
   220→
   221→    for _, rect in ipairs(rectangles) do
   222→        p1.x, p1.y = math.max(p1.x, rect.x),  math.min(p1.y, rect.y)
   223→        p2.x, p2.y = math.min(p2.x, rect.x +  rect.width),  math.max(p2.y, rect.y + rect.height)
   224→    end
   225→
   226→    -- Never try to paint this, it would freeze the system.
   227→    assert(p1.y ~= math.huge and p2.a ~= math.huge, "Setting wallpaper failed")
   228→
   229→    return {
   230→        x      = p1.x,
   231→        y      = p1.y,
   232→        width  = p2.x - p1.x,
   233→        height = p2.y - p1.y,
   234→    }
   235→end
   236→
   237→-- Best or vertical and horizontal "inner" modes.
   238→function panning_modes.inner(self)
   239→    local vert = panning_modes.inner_vertical(self)
   240→    local hori = panning_modes.inner_horizontal(self)
   241→
   242→    if vert.width <= 0 or vert.height <= 0 then return hori end
   243→    if hori.width <= 0 or hori.height <= 0 then return vert end
   244→
   245→    if vert.width * vert.height > hori.width * hori.height then
   246→        return vert
   247→    else
   248→        return hori
   249→    end
   250→end

   253→local function paint()
   254→    if not next(pending_repaint) then return end
   255→
   256→    local root_width, root_height = capi.root.size()
   257→
   258→    -- Get the current wallpaper content.
   259→    local source = surface(root.wallpaper())
   260→
   261→    local target, cr
   262→
   263→    -- It's possible that a wallpaper for 1 screen is set using another tool, so make
   264→    -- sure we copy the current content.
   265→    if source then
   266→        target = source:create_similar(cairo.Content.COLOR, root_width, root_height)
   267→        cr     = cairo.Context(target)
   268→
   269→        -- Copy the old wallpaper to the new one
   270→        cr:save()
   271→        cr.operator = cairo.Operator.SOURCE
   272→        cr:set_source_surface(source, 0, 0)
   273→
   274→        for s in screen do
   275→            cr:rectangle(
   276→                s.geometry.x,
   277→                s.geometry.y,
   278→                s.geometry.width,
   279→                s.geometry.height
   280→            )
   281→        end
   282→
   283→        cr:clip()
   284→
   285→        cr:paint()
   286→        cr:restore()
   287→    else
   288→        target = cairo.ImageSurface(cairo.Format.RGB32, root_width, root_height)
   289→        cr     = cairo.Context(target)
   290→    end
   291→
   292→    local walls = {}
   293→
   294→    for _, wall in pairs(backgrounds) do
   295→        walls[wall] = true
   296→    end
   297→
   298→    -- Not supposed to happen, but there is enough API surface for
   299→    -- it to be a side effect of some signals. Calling the panning
   300→    -- mode callback with zero screen is not supported.
   301→    if not next(walls) then
   302→        return
   303→    end
   304→
   305→    for wall in pairs(walls) do
   306→
   307→        local geo = type(wall._private.panning_area) == "function" and
   308→            wall._private.panning_area(wall) or
   309→            panning_modes[wall._private.panning_area](wall)
   310→
   311→        -- If false, this panning area isn't well suited for the screen geometry.
   312→        if geo.width > 0 or geo.height > 0 then
   313→            local uncovered_areas = grect.area_remove(get_rectangles(wall.screens, false, false), geo)
   314→
   315→            cr:save()
   316→
   317→            -- Prevent overwrite then there is multiple non-continuous screens.
   318→            for _, s in ipairs(wall.screens) do
   319→                cr:rectangle(
   320→                    s.geometry.x,
   321→                    s.geometry.y,
   322→                    s.geometry.width,
   323→                    s.geometry.height
   324→                )
   325→            end
   326→
   327→            cr:clip()
   328→
   329→            -- The older surface might contain garbage, optionally clean it.
   330→            if wall.uncovered_areas_color then
   331→                cr:set_source(gcolor(wall.uncovered_areas_color))
   332→
   333→                for _, area in ipairs(uncovered_areas) do
   334→                    cr:rectangle(area.x, area.y, area.width, area.height)
   335→                    cr:fill()
   336→                end
   337→            end
   338→
   339→            if not wall._private.container then
   340→                wall._private.container = background()
   341→                wall._private.container.bg = wall._private.bg or beautiful.wallpaper_bg or "#000000"
   342→                wall._private.container.fg = wall._private.fg or beautiful.wallpaper_fg or "#ffffff"
   343→                wall._private.container.widget = wall.widget
   344→            end
   345→
   346→            local a_context = {
   347→                dpi = wall._private.context.dpi
   348→            }
   349→
   350→            -- Pick the lowest DPI.
   351→            if not a_context.dpi then
   352→                a_context.dpi = math.huge
   353→                for _, s in ipairs(wall.screens) do
   354→                    a_context.dpi = math.min(
   355→                        s.dpi and s.dpi or s.preferred_dpi, a_context.dpi
   356→                    )
   357→                end
   358→            end
   359→
   360→            -- Fallback.
   361→            if not a_context.dpi then
   362→                a_context.dpi = 96
   363→            end
   364→
   365→            cr:translate(geo.x, geo.y)
   366→            draw(wall._private.container, cr, geo.width, geo.height, a_context)
   367→            cr:restore()
   368→        end
   369→    end
   370→
   371→    -- Set the wallpaper.
   372→    local pattern = cairo.Pattern.create_for_surface(target)
   373→    capi.root.wallpaper(pattern)
   374→
   375→    -- Limit some potential GC induced increase in memory usage.
   376→    -- But really, is someone is trying to apply wallpaper changes more
   377→    -- often than the GC is executed, they are doing it wrong.
   378→    target:finish()
   379→
   380→end

   382→local mutex = false
   383→
   384→-- Uploading the surface to X11 is *very* resource intensive. Given the updates
   385→-- will often happen in batch (like startup), make sure to only do one "real"
   386→-- update.
   387→local function update()
   388→    if mutex then return end
   389→
   390→    mutex = true
   391→
   392→    gtimer.delayed_call(function()
   393→        -- Remove the mutex first in case `paint()` raises an exception.
   394→        mutex = false
   395→        paint()
   396→    end)
   397→end

   399→capi.screen.connect_signal("removed", function(s)
   400→    if not backgrounds[s] then return end
   401→
   402→    backgrounds[s]:remove_screen(s)
   403→
   404→    update()
   405→end)
   406→
   407→capi.screen.connect_signal("property::geometry", function(s)
   408→    if not backgrounds[s] then return end
   409→
   410→    backgrounds[s]:repaint()
   411→end)

   563→-- @tparam[opt="transparent"] color uncovered_areas_color

   566→--- Defines where the wallpaper is placed when there is multiple screens.
   567→--
   568→-- When there is more than 1 screen, it is possible they don't have the same
   569→-- resolution, position or orientation. Panning the wallpaper over them may look
   570→-- better if a continuous rectangle is used rather than creating a virtual rectangle
   571→-- around all screens.
   572→--
   573→-- The default algorithms are:
   574→--
   575→-- **outer:** *(default)*
   576→--
   577→-- Draw an imaginary rectangle around all screens.
   578→--
   579→-- @DOC_awful_wallpaper_panning_outer_EXAMPLE@
   580→--
   581→-- **inner:**
   582→--
   583→-- Take the largest area or either `inner_horizontal` or `inner_vertical`.
   584→--
   585→-- @DOC_awful_wallpaper_panning_inner_EXAMPLE@
   586→--
   587→-- **inner_horizontal:**
   588→--
   589→-- Take the smallest `x` value, the largest `x+width`, the smallest `y`
   590→-- and the smallest `y+height`.
   591→--
   592→-- @DOC_awful_wallpaper_panning_inner_horizontal_EXAMPLE@
   593→--
   594→-- **inner_vertical:**
   595→--
   596→-- Take the smallest `y` value, the largest `y+height`, the smallest `x`
   597→-- and the smallest `x+width`.
   598→--
   599→-- @DOC_awful_wallpaper_panning_inner_vertical_EXAMPLE@
   600→--
   601→-- **Custom function:**
   602→--
   603→-- It is also possible to define a custom function.
   604→--
   605→-- @DOC_awful_wallpaper_panning_custom_EXAMPLE@
   606→--
   607→-- @property panning_area
   608→-- @tparam[opt="outer"] function|string panning_area
   609→-- @propertytype string A panning algorithm
   610→-- @propertyvalue "outer"
   611→-- @propertyvalue "inner"
   612→-- @propertyvalue "inner_horizontal"
   613→-- @propertyvalue "inner_vertical"
   614→-- @propertytype function Custom panning function.
   615→-- @functionparam awful.wallpaper wallpaper The wallpaper object.
   616→-- @functionreturn A table with `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` keys,
   617→-- @see uncovered_areas
   618→
   619→function module:set_panning_area(value)
   620→    value = value or "outer"
   621→
   622→    assert(type(value) == "function" or panning_modes[value], "Invalid panning mode: "..tostring(value))
   623→
   624→    self._private.panning_area = value
   625→
   626→    self:repaint()
   627→
   628→    self:emit_signal("property::panning_area", value)
   629→end

   673→function module:get_uncovered_areas()
   674→    local geo = type(self._private.panning_area) == "function" and
   675→        self._private.panning_area(self) or
   676→        panning_modes[self._private.panning_area](self)
   677→
   678→    return grect.area_remove(get_rectangles(self.screens, false, false), geo)

   681→function module:set_screens(screens)
   682→    local to_rem = {}
   683→
   684→    -- All screens.
   685→    -- The copy is needed because it's a metatable, `ipairs` doesn't work
   686→    -- correctly in all Lua versions.
   687→    if screens == capi.screen then
   688→        screens = {}
   689→
   690→        for s in capi.screen do
   691→            table.insert(screens, s)
   692→        end
   693→    end
   694→
   695→    for _, s in ipairs(screens) do
   696→        to_rem[get_screen(s)] = true
   697→    end
   698→
   699→    for _, s in ipairs(self.screens) do
   700→        to_rem[get_screen(s)] = nil
   701→    end
   702→
   703→    for _, s in ipairs(screens) do
   704→        s = get_screen(s)
   705→        self:add_screen(s)
   706→        to_rem[s] = nil
   707→    end
   708→
   709→    for s, remove in pairs(to_rem) do
   710→        if remove then
   711→            self:remove_screen(s)
   712→        end
   713→    end
   714→end
   715→
   716→function module:get_screens()
   717→    return self._private.screens
   718→end

   725→--

   759→-- Adding a new wallpaper to a screen will automatically

   785→-- automatically repainted. Repainting the native X11 wallpaper is slow and

   787→-- really need to repaint the wallpaper, call this method.

   799→--- Remove a screen.
   800→--
   801→-- Calling this will remove a screen, but will **not** repaint its area.
   802→-- In this example, the wallpaper was spanning all 3 screens and the
   803→-- first screen was removed:
   804→--
   805→-- @DOC_awful_wallpaper_remove_screen1_EXAMPLE@
   806→--
   807→-- As you can see, the content of screen 1 still looks like it is part of
   808→-- the 3 screen wallpaper. The only use case for calling this method is if
   809→-- you use a 3rd party tools to change the wallpaper.
   810→--
   811→-- If you wish to simply remove a screen and not have leftover content, it is
   812→-- simpler to just create a new wallpaper for that screen:
   813→--
   814→-- @DOC_awful_wallpaper_remove_screen2_EXAMPLE@
   815→--
   816→-- @method remove_screen
   817→-- @tparam screen screen The screen to remove.
   818→-- @treturn boolean `true` if the screen was removed and `false` if the screen
   819→--  wasn't found.
   820→-- @see detach
   821→-- @see add_screen
   822→-- @see screens
   823→function module:remove_screen(s)
   824→    local ret =  false
   825→
   826→    s = get_screen(s)
   827→
   828→    for k, s2 in ipairs(self._private.screens) do
   829→        if s == s2 then
   830→            table.remove(self._private.screens, k)
   831→            ret = true
   832→        end
   833→    end
   834→
   835→    backgrounds[s] = nil
   836→
   837→    self:repaint()
   838→
   839→    return ret
   840→end

   842→--- Create a wallpaper.
   843→--
   844→-- Note that all parameters are not required. Please refer to the
   845→-- module description and examples to understand parameters usages.
   846→--
   847→-- @constructorfct awful.wallpaper
   848→-- @tparam table args
   849→-- @tparam[opt] wibox.widget args.widget The wallpaper widget.
   850→-- @tparam[opt] number args.dpi The wallpaper DPI (dots per inch).
   851→-- @tparam[opt] screen args.screen The wallpaper screen.
   852→-- @tparam[opt] table args.screens A list of screen for this wallpaper.
   853→--  Use this parameter as a remplacement for `args.screen` to manage multiscreen wallpaper.
   854→--  (Note: the expected table should be an array-like table `{screen1, screen2, ...}`)
   855→-- @tparam[opt] gears.color args.bg The background color.
   856→-- @tparam[opt] gears.color args.fg The foreground color.
   857→-- @tparam[opt] gears.color args.uncovered_areas_color The color for the uncovered areas.
   858→-- @tparam[opt] boolean args.honor_workarea Honor the workarea.
   859→-- @tparam[opt] boolean args.honor_padding Honor the screen padding.
   860→-- @tparam[opt] table args.uncovered_areas Returns the list of screen(s) area which won't be covered by the wallpaper.
   861→-- @tparam[opt] function|string args.panning_area Defines where the wallpaper is placed when there is multiple screens.
   862→
   863→local function new(_, args)
   864→    args = args or {}
   865→    local ret = gobject {
   866→        enable_auto_signals = true,
   867→        enable_properties   = true,
   868→    }
   869→
   870→    rawset(ret, "_private", {})
   871→    ret._private.context      = {}
   872→    ret._private.panning_area = "outer"
   873→
   874→    gtable.crush(ret, module, true)
   875→
   876→    ret:_clear()

# SomeWM Wallpaper Caching Documentation

## Overview

The page documents SomeWM's wallpaper caching system, which optimizes performance when switching wallpapers across different tags by caching GPU textures rather than reloading from disk each time.

## The Problem

Tag switching without caching involves five expensive steps: loading images (~5ms), creating cairo surfaces (~2ms), scaling (~3ms), uploading GPU textures (~5ms), and destroying old textures. This totals "~15-25ms per switch," which exceeds the 16.6ms frame budget at 60fps, causing visible lag.

## Performance Impact

The caching mechanism provides dramatic speedup:

| Operation | Without Cache | With Cache |
|-----------|---------------|-----------|
| First visit | ~20ms | ~20ms |
| Subsequent visits | ~20ms | **~0.1ms** |
| Speedup | — | **~200x** |

## How It Works

### Two-Level Caching Strategy

1. **GPU Texture Level**: SomeWM maintains cached scene nodes instead of destroying wallpaper textures. Switching involves toggling visibility rather than recreating buffers.

2. **Lua Level**: The system patches `gears.wallpaper.maximized()` to check the cache before executing expensive operations like file I/O and image decoding.

The patched version returns immediately on cache hits, "bypassing" file I/O, image decoding, cairo surface creation, scaling, painting, and pattern creation.

### Per-Screen Caching

Wallpapers cache using `(path, screen_index)` as the key. Each entry's scene node positions at screen coordinates and matches screen dimensions. This allows independent wallpaper switching on multi-monitor setups.

## Cache Operations

| Operation | Complexity | Description |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| Lookup | O(n) | Linear scan by filepath and screen |
| Insert | O(1) | Add to list head |
| Evict | O(n) | Remove oldest unused entry |
| Show | O(1) | Toggle visibility flags |

## Memory Requirements

Per cached wallpaper: width × height × 4 bytes (ARGB32)

Examples:
- 1920×1080: ~8 MB
- 3840×2160: ~32 MB

With maximum 32 cached entries:
- Dual-monitor setup (18 wallpapers): ~144 MB (1080p) or ~576 MB (4K)

## Implementation Details

### Monkey-Patching Approach

SomeWM intercepts `require('gears.wallpaper')` at startup, wrapping the `maximized` function without modifying source files.

### Cache Key Mechanism

Filepath strings serve as cache keys. This means:
- Identical paths = cache hit
- Different paths to same file = cache miss
- Modified files create stale cache entries

## Supported Wallpaper Functions

**Currently Cached:**
- `gears.wallpaper.maximized()`

**Not Cached:**
- `gears.wallpaper.centered()`
- `gears.wallpaper.tiled()`
- `gears.wallpaper.fit()`

## Caching Requirements

- Cache keys require file path strings: `gears.wallpaper.maximized("/path/to/image.jpg", s, true)`
- Cairo surface objects cannot be cached without file paths

## LRU Eviction

When the 32-entry limit is reached, the least recently used wallpaper not currently displayed on any screen is evicted, freeing its GPU resources.

## Cache Invalidation

The cache doesn't detect file modifications on disk. Users must either restart SomeWM or manually call `root.wallpaper_cache_clear()`.

1. **Upstream wallpaper caching** works transparently - it monkey-patches `gears.wallpaper.maximized()` to intercept the call and check the cache. If cached, it toggles scene node visibility (0.1ms). If not cached, it falls through to the original implementation and adds to cache.

3. **The caching should work transparently** because the monkey-patch intercepts the function calls and uses file paths as cache keys, with per-screen caching handled through the screen argument.

4. **There's a potential issue**: the user's Lua-level `s.current_wallpaper` check might actually bypass the cache entirely—if it skips calling `gears.wallpaper.maximized()` when the wallpaper hasn't changed, the cache never gets invoked in the first place.

But actually, that's not a problem because the cache only matters when switching between different wallpapers. When toggling back to a previously-used wallpaper on the same screen, the cache hits and provides instant switching, while the user's tracking just prevents unnecessary calls when nothing actually changes.

The real optimization opportunity here is pre-caching all the wallpapers at startup using `root.wallpaper_cache_preload()` to eliminate even the first-switch delay entirely. Let me verify if that API is actually available in the codebase.

content.text:
Mam vsechny informace. Tady je analyza:

## Jak funguje upstream caching

Upstream pridal **transparentni cache system** — monkey-patchuje `gears.wallpaper.maximized()` automaticky pri startu. Kdyz zavolass `gears.wallpaper.maximized(path, screen, ...)`:

1. **Cache hit** → prepne viditelnost GPU scene nodu (~0.1ms)
2. **Cache miss** → nahraje obrazek, ulozi do cache, zobrazi (~20ms)

## Tvuj rc.lua je uz kompatibilni

Tvuj kod na radcich 256-263:
```lua
local function set_wallpaper(scr, wallpaper_file)
    if scr.current_wallpaper == wallpaper_file then return end
    local wp = wppath .. wallpaper_file
    gears.wallpaper.maximized(wp, scr, false)  -- ← cache tohle zachyti automaticky
    scr.current_wallpaper = wallpaper_file
end
```

Tohle uz funguje spravne. Pouzivas filepath string + screen objekt, coz je presne to co cache ocekava. Tvuj Lua-level guard (`current_wallpaper`) je bonusova optimalizace navic — zabraní i volani funkce kdyz se wallpaper nemeni.

Jedine co bychom mohli pridat je **pre-caching** pri startu, aby i prvni prepnuti na kazdy tag bylo okamzite. Overim ze API existuje.

#!/bin/bash
# ============================================================================
# Session launcher - TUI menu for starting desktop sessions from TTY
# ============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

# ── Colors & Drawing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Gruvbox-inspired palette
C_BG="\033[48;5;235m"       # dark bg
C_FG="\033[38;5;223m"       # light fg
C_DIM="\033[38;5;245m"      # dimmed
C_ACCENT="\033[38;5;214m"   # orange accent
C_ACCENT2="\033[38;5;142m"  # green accent
C_ACCENT3="\033[38;5;109m"  # blue accent
C_ACCENT4="\033[38;5;175m"  # purple accent
C_SEL_BG="\033[48;5;237m"   # selected bg
C_SEL_FG="\033[38;5;214m"   # selected fg
C_BOLD="\033[1m"
C_RESET="\033[0m"
C_HIDE="\033[?25l"
C_SHOW="\033[?25h"
C_CLEAR="\033[2J\033[H"

# Box drawing
H="─"  V="│"  TL="╭"  TR="╮"  BL="╰"  BR="╯"

# ── Session definitions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Format: "id|name|description|type|command"
#   type: wayland, x11, script

SESSIONS=(
    "somewm|somewm|Wayland compositor (wlroots)|wayland|somewm-session"
    "kde|KDE Plasma|Wayland desktop environment|wayland|/usr/lib/plasma-dbus-run-session-if-needed /usr/bin/startplasma-wayland"
    "awesome|AwesomeWM|X11 window manager (via .xinitrc)|x11|$HOME/.xinitrc awesome"
    "hyprland|Hyprland|Wayland compositor (wlroots)|wayland|dbus-run-session Hyprland"
)

# Filter to only sessions whose binary exists
AVAILABLE=()
for entry in "${SESSIONS[@]}"; do
    IFS='|' read -r id name desc type cmd <<< "$entry"
    # Check first word of command
    local_bin="${cmd%% *}"
    if command -v "$local_bin" &>/dev/null || [ -x "$local_bin" ]; then
        AVAILABLE+=("$entry")
    fi
done

if [ ${#AVAILABLE[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "No sessions available."
    exit 1
fi

# ── Drawing functions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

get_term_size() {
    LINES=$(tput lines)
    COLS=$(tput cols)
}

# Print at position
at() { printf "\033[%d;%dH" "$1" "$2"; }

# Draw horizontal line
hline() {
    local y=$1 x=$2 len=$3 color=${4:-$C_DIM}
    at "$y" "$x"
    printf "%b" "$color"
    printf "%0.s$H" $(seq 1 "$len")
    printf "%b" "$C_RESET"
}

# Draw box
box() {
    local y=$1 x=$2 w=$3 h=$4 color=${5:-$C_DIM}
    at "$y" "$x"; printf "%b%s" "$color" "$TL"
    printf "%0.s$H" $(seq 1 $((w-2)))
    printf "%s%b" "$TR" "$C_RESET"

    for ((i=1; i<h-1; i++)); do
        at $((y+i)) "$x"; printf "%b%s%b" "$color" "$V" "$C_RESET"
        at $((y+i)) $((x+w-1)); printf "%b%s%b" "$color" "$V" "$C_RESET"
    done

    at $((y+h-1)) "$x"; printf "%b%s" "$color" "$BL"
    printf "%0.s$H" $(seq 1 $((w-2)))
    printf "%s%b" "$BR" "$C_RESET"
}

# Center text in given width
center() {
    local text="$1" width=$2
    local len=${#text}
    local pad=$(( (width - len) / 2 ))
    printf "%*s%s%*s" "$pad" "" "$text" $((width - len - pad)) ""
}

# ── ASCII Art ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

draw_logo() {
    local y=$1 x=$2
    local O=$'\033[38;5;214m'   # orange (sloth)
    local B=$'\033[38;5;172m'   # brown (nose)
    local W=$'\033[38;5;223m'   # warm white (face)
    local D=$'\033[38;5;239m'   # dim (feet)
    local R=$'\033[0m'

    local -a lines=()
    lines+=("${W}   --(( ${W}----${W} ))--${R}")
    lines+=("${O}      \\\\     /|${R}")
    lines+=("${W}   p${B}*${W}q${O}/  \\_/  \\\\${R}")
    lines+=("${O}   \\\\          /${R}")
    lines+=("${O}    \" _     _\"${R}")
    lines+=("${O}        —  —${R}")
    local i=0
    for line in "${lines[@]}"; do
        at $((y + i)) "$x"
        printf "%s" "$line"
        ((i+=1))
    done

    # Motto centered independently
    local motto="\"Chces slyset vtip, Blesku?\""
    at $((y + i + 1)) $(( x - 3 ))
    printf "%s" "${D}${motto}${R}"
}

draw_wm_name() {
    local y=$1 x=$2 id=$3
    local A=$'\033[38;5;214m'
    local R=$'\033[0m'

    local -a art=()
    case "$id" in
        somewm)
            art+=(' ___  ___  _ __ ___   _____      ___ __ ___  ')
            art+=('/ __|/ _ \| '"'"'_ ` _ \ / _ \ \ /\ / / '"'"'_ ` _ \ ')
            art+=('\__ \ (_) | | | | | |  __/\ V  V /| | | | | |')
            art+=('|___/\___/|_| |_| |_|\___| \_/\_/ |_| |_| |_|')
            ;;
        kde)
            art+=(' _  _____  ___   ___ _                    ')
            art+=('| |/ /   \| __| | _ \ |__ _ ____ __  __ _ ')
            art+=('| '"'"' <| |) | _|  |  _/ / _` (_-< '"'"'  \/ _` |')
            art+=('|_|\_\___/|___| |_| |_\__,_/__/_|_|_\__,_|')
            ;;
        awesome)
            art+=('   _                             __      ____  __ ')
            art+=('  /_\__ __ _____ ___ ___ _ __  __\ \    / /  \/  |')
            art+=(' / _ \ V  V / -_|_-</ _ \ '"'"'  \/ -_) \/\/ /| |\/| |')
            art+=('/_/ \_\_/\_/\___/__/\___/_|_|_\___|\_/\_/ |_|  |_|')
            ;;
        hyprland)
            art+=(' _  _               _              _ ')
            art+=('| || |_  _ _ __ _ _| |__ _ _ _  __| |')
            art+=('| __ | || | '"'"'_ \ '"'"'_| / _` | '"'"' \/ _` |')
            art+=('|_||_|\_, | .__/_| |_\__,_|_||_\__,_|')
            art+=('      |__/|_|                        ')
            ;;
    esac

    local i=0
    for line in "${art[@]}"; do
        at $((y + i)) "$x"
        printf "%s%s%s" "$A" "$line" "$R"
        ((i+=1))
    done
}

draw_system_info() {
    local y=$1 x=$2 w=$3
    local kernel hostname uptime_str mem_str

    kernel=$(uname -r | sed 's/-.*//')
    hostname=$(uname -n)
    uptime_str=$(uptime -p 2>/dev/null | sed 's/up //' || echo "?")
    mem_str=$(free -h 2>/dev/null | awk '/Mem:/{print $3"/"$2}' || echo "?")

    at "$y" "$x"
    printf "%b%b%s%b  %b%s%b  %b%s%b  %b%s%b" \
        "$C_DIM" \
        "$C_ACCENT3" "⬡ $hostname" "$C_DIM" \
        "$C_ACCENT2" "⚙ $kernel" "$C_DIM" \
        "$C_ACCENT4" "↑ $uptime_str" "$C_DIM" \
        "$C_ACCENT" "▪ $mem_str" "$C_RESET"
}

# ── Menu ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

draw_menu() {
    local selected=$1
    local box_w=56
    local box_x=$(( (COLS - box_w) / 2 ))
    local box_y=20
    local item_count=${#AVAILABLE[@]}
    local box_h=$(( item_count * 3 + 4 ))

    # Box
    box "$box_y" "$box_x" "$box_w" "$box_h" "$C_DIM"

    # Title
    at "$box_y" $((box_x + 2))
    printf "%b%b %s %b" "$C_DIM" "$C_BOLD$C_ACCENT" "SELECT SESSION" "$C_RESET"

    # Items
    local idx=0
    for entry in "${AVAILABLE[@]}"; do
        IFS='|' read -r id name desc type cmd <<< "$entry"
        local iy=$((box_y + 2 + idx * 3))

        # Type badge
        local badge badge_color
        case "$type" in
            wayland) badge="WL"  ; badge_color="$C_ACCENT2";;
            x11)     badge="X11" ; badge_color="$C_ACCENT4";;
            script)  badge="SH"  ; badge_color="$C_ACCENT3";;
        esac

        if [ "$idx" -eq "$selected" ]; then
            # Selected item - highlighted
            at "$iy" $((box_x + 2))
            printf "%b%b  ▸ %b%-20s %b[%s]%b" \
                "$C_SEL_BG" "$C_SEL_FG" "$C_BOLD" "$name" "$badge_color" "$badge" "$C_RESET"
            at $((iy + 1)) $((box_x + 2))
            printf "%b%b    %-48s%b" \
                "$C_SEL_BG" "$C_FG" "$desc" "$C_RESET"
        else
            # Normal item
            at "$iy" $((box_x + 2))
            printf "%b    %-20s %b[%s]%b" \
                "$C_DIM" "$name" "$badge_color" "$badge" "$C_RESET"
            at $((iy + 1)) $((box_x + 2))
            printf "%b    %-48s%b" \
                "\033[38;5;241m" "$desc" "$C_RESET"
        fi

        ((idx+=1))
    done

    # Footer
    local footer_y=$((box_y + box_h))
    at "$footer_y" "$box_x"
    printf "%b  ↑↓ navigate  ⏎ launch  q quit%b" "$C_DIM" "$C_RESET"
}

# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cleanup() {
    printf "%b%b" "$C_SHOW" "$C_RESET"
    tput cnorm 2>/dev/null
    stty sane 2>/dev/null
    clear
}
trap cleanup EXIT

main() {
    get_term_size

    # Hide cursor
    printf "%b%b" "$C_HIDE" "$C_CLEAR"

    local selected=0
    local item_count=${#AVAILABLE[@]}

    while true; do
        # Clear and draw
        printf "%b" "$C_CLEAR"

        # Logo centered
        local logo_w=30
        local logo_x=$(( (COLS - logo_w) / 2 ))
        draw_logo 2 "$logo_x"

        # WM name ASCII art (below motto)
        local sel_entry="${AVAILABLE[$selected]}"
        local sel_id
        IFS='|' read -r sel_id _ _ _ _ <<< "$sel_entry"
        local wm_art_w=52
        draw_wm_name 12 $(( (COLS - wm_art_w) / 2 )) "$sel_id"

        # System info
        draw_system_info 18 $(( (COLS - 60) / 2 )) 60

        # Menu
        draw_menu "$selected"

        # Read key (bash read -rsn1 works on both TTY and pty)
        local key
        IFS= read -rsn1 key

        case "$key" in
            $'\x1b')
                # Escape sequence - read remaining bytes with timeout
                # Arrow keys send \x1b[A etc. Bare Escape = nothing follows
                local seq
                IFS= read -rsn2 -t 0.1 seq || true
                case "$seq" in
                    "[A") # Up
                        selected=$(( (selected - 1 + item_count) % item_count ))
                        ;;
                    "[B") # Down
                        selected=$(( (selected + 1) % item_count ))
                        ;;
                    "") # Bare Escape (no follow-up bytes)
                        exit 0
                        ;;
                esac
                ;;
            "") # Enter
                # Launch selected session
                local entry="${AVAILABLE[$selected]}"
                IFS='|' read -r id name desc type cmd <<< "$entry"

                # Restore terminal
                cleanup
                trap - EXIT

                echo "Launching $name..."
                sleep 0.3

                case "$type" in
                    x11)
                        exec startx $cmd
                        ;;
                    wayland|script)
                        exec $cmd
                        ;;
                esac
                ;;
            "q"|"Q") # Quit
                exit 0
                ;;
            "k") # vim up
                selected=$(( (selected - 1 + item_count) % item_count ))
                ;;
            "j") # vim down
                selected=$(( (selected + 1) % item_count ))
                ;;
        esac
    done
}

#!/bin/bash
# somewm session launcher with restart and rebuild support
# Exit codes: 0=quit, 1=restart, 2=rebuild+restart
#
# Two modes:
#   1) Dev mode:  SOMEWM_DIR=/path/to/somewm somewm-session
#                 Uses build/somewm binary and ./lua modules
#   2) Installed: somewm-session
#                 Uses system-installed somewm from PATH

# Load environment.d configs (same files systemd reads for DM sessions)
for _conf in "$HOME/.config/environment.d/"*.conf; do
    [ -f "$_conf" ] || continue
    set -a
    . "$_conf"
    set +a
done
unset _conf

# Use the systemd user bus (where gnome-keyring and other services live).
# dbus-broker provides this automatically via /run/user/$UID/bus.
export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS:-unix:path=/run/user/$(id -u)/bus}"

# Start gnome-keyring (secrets/pkcs11 only - SSH agent is handled by gcr-ssh-agent).
# PAM auto-unlocks it at TTY login (pam_gnome_keyring.so).
if command -v gnome-keyring-daemon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    eval $(gnome-keyring-daemon --start --components=pkcs11,secrets 2>/dev/null)
fi

# SSH agent via gcr-ssh-agent (gnome-keyring dropped SSH in v46+)
export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="${SSH_AUTH_SOCK:-/run/user/$(id -u)/gcr/ssh}"

# Import environment into systemd and dbus so child processes and portals see it
systemctl --user import-environment DISPLAY WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP SSH_AUTH_SOCK 2>/dev/null

SOMEWM_LOG="${HOME}/.local/log/somewm-debug.log"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$SOMEWM_LOG")"

if [ -n "$SOMEWM_DIR" ]; then
    # Dev mode: run from build directory
    SOMEWM_BIN="${SOMEWM_DIR}/build/somewm"
    SOMEWM_ARGS=(-d -L "${SOMEWM_DIR}/lua")

    if [ ! -x "$SOMEWM_BIN" ]; then
        echo "Binary not found: $SOMEWM_BIN"
        echo "Run 'ninja -C ${SOMEWM_DIR}/build' first."
        exit 1
    fi
else
    # Installed mode: use system binary
    SOMEWM_BIN="$(command -v somewm)"
    SOMEWM_ARGS=(-d)

    if [ -z "$SOMEWM_BIN" ]; then
        echo "somewm not found in PATH."
        echo "Install with 'sudo ninja -C build install' or set SOMEWM_DIR."
        exit 1
    fi
fi

while true; do
    "$SOMEWM_BIN" "${SOMEWM_ARGS[@]}" 2>&1 \
        | tee "$SOMEWM_LOG"
    exit_code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

    case $exit_code in
        0)
            echo "somewm exited normally."
            break
            ;;
        2)
            if [ -n "$SOMEWM_DIR" ]; then
                echo "Rebuilding somewm..."
                if ! ninja -C "${SOMEWM_DIR}/build"; then
                    echo "Build failed! Restarting with old binary..."
                fi
            else
                echo "Rebuild requested but SOMEWM_DIR not set, skipping build."
            fi
            echo "Restarting in 1s..."
            sleep 1
            ;;
        *)
            echo "somewm exited ($exit_code), restarting in 1s..."
            sleep 1
            ;;
    esac
done

content.thinking:
The user is right. If we use `exec ~/bin/session-launcher` in `.bash_profile`, then when the user presses 'q' in session-launcher, the shell process is replaced by session-launcher, so when session-launcher exits, the login session ends and goes back to the login prompt — creating an annoying loop.

The fix: don't use `exec` for the session-launcher call. Just call it directly. When the user quits (q), they'll get a normal bash shell on the TTY.

Wait, but looking at the session-launcher script, when a session is selected it uses `exec $cmd` which replaces the session-launcher process. 

Actually, I need to trace through this more carefully. When session-launcher does `exec $cmd` to launch the window manager, that replaces the session-launcher process entirely. So if we don't use `exec` in `.bash_profile`, the chain becomes: bash calls session-launcher, which then execs into the window manager. When the window manager exits, control returns to bash since session-launcher was replaced by exec. That's the right behavior.

- High-resolution scroll events (smooth scrolling) being handled differently
- Scroll events being consumed/accumulated differently on wibar widgets
- The wibar widget might be receiving discrete AND smooth scroll events, causing double-counting or event loss

Now I need to dig into the codebase to see how these scroll events are actually being processed.

1→# Fix: Titlebar geometry, surface clipping, and pointer focus
     2→
     3→**Issue:** https://github.com/trip-zip/somewm/issues/230
     4→**Fork branch:** https://github.com/raven2cz/somewm/tree/fix/titlebar-geometry-clipping-and-pointer-focus
     5→**Commits:**
     6→- [`f213c3e`](https://github.com/raven2cz/somewm/commit/f213c3e) fix: surface clip accounts for titlebars and border width
     7→- [`826c64b`](https://github.com/raven2cz/somewm/commit/826c64b) fix: titlebar-aware geometry bounds and fullscreen rendering
     8→- [`997d308`](https://github.com/raven2cz/somewm/commit/997d308) fix: pointer focus over titlebars, borders, and on client map
     9→- [`754d127`](https://github.com/raven2cz/somewm/commit/754d127) feat: client aspect ratio constraint for resize
    10→
    11→## Summary
    12→
    13→Multiple interrelated bugs cause incorrect rendering, lost pointer focus, and
    14→crashes when using clients with titlebars (mpv, GNOME Calculator, any client
    15→with `awful.titlebar`). The root cause is that the compositor's C-side geometry,
    16→clipping, and pointer focus code was written before titlebars were fully
    17→integrated, and never updated to account for the space titlebars occupy inside
    18→client geometry.
    19→
    20→**Affected clients:** Any client with titlebars enabled (mpv, GNOME Calculator,
    21→Nautilus, etc.), and fullscreen clients that previously had titlebars.
    22→
    23→## Bug 1: Surface bleeds past bottom/right borders (visual corruption)
    24→
    25→### Symptoms
    26→- Bottom border appears to "creep into" the application content
    27→- At small window sizes, the bottom border visually overlaps the app
    28→- The effect is exactly `titlebar_top` pixels (typically 29px) of overflow
    29→
    30→### Root Cause
    31→
    32→`client_get_clip()` in `client.h` computes the clip rectangle that restricts
    33→how much of the client surface is visible. The surface scene node is positioned
    34→at `(bw + titlebar_left, bw + titlebar_top)` within the parent, but the clip
    35→dimensions were `geometry - bw` instead of `geometry - 2*bw - titlebars`:
    36→
    37→```c
    38→// BEFORE (wrong):
    39→.width = c->geometry.width - c->bw,
    40→.height = c->geometry.height - c->bw,
    41→
    42→// The visible bottom edge in parent coords becomes:
    43→//   bw + titlebar_top + (geometry.height - bw) = titlebar_top + geometry.height
    44→// This extends titlebar_top pixels PAST the bottom of the window!
    45→```
    46→
    47→### Fix
    48→
    49→**File:** `client.h` - `client_get_clip()`
    50→
    51→Compute clip as the content area size (geometry minus borders minus all four
    52→titlebars), with fullscreen handling (titlebars are hidden in fullscreen):
    53→
    54→```c
    55→int tl = c->fullscreen ? 0 : c->titlebar[CLIENT_TITLEBAR_LEFT].size;
    56→int tt = c->fullscreen ? 0 : c->titlebar[CLIENT_TITLEBAR_TOP].size;
    57→int tr = c->fullscreen ? 0 : c->titlebar[CLIENT_TITLEBAR_RIGHT].size;
    58→int tb = c->fullscreen ? 0 : c->titlebar[CLIENT_TITLEBAR_BOTTOM].size;
    59→int cw = c->geometry.width - 2 * c->bw - tl - tr;
    60→int ch = c->geometry.height - 2 * c->bw - tt - tb;
    61→if (cw < 1) cw = 1;
    62→if (ch < 1) ch = 1;
    63→```
    64→
    65→Now the visible area correctly ends at `(geometry.width - bw - tr, geometry.height - bw - tb)` -- exactly adjacent to the borders.
    66→
    67→## Bug 2: Crash on extreme resize (unsigned integer underflow)
    68→
    69→### Symptoms
    70→- Resizing a window with titlebars to very small sizes crashes the compositor
    71→- The crash occurs in wlroots when it receives huge width/height values
    72→- Only affects windows with titlebars; windows without titlebars hit a
    73→  reasonable minimum of `1 + 2*bw = 3px`
    74→
    75→### Root Cause
    76→
    77→Two issues in `somewm.c`:
    78→
    79→1. **`applybounds()`** enforced minimum geometry of `1 + 2*bw` (e.g., 3px) but
    80→   didn't account for titlebar sizes. A window with a 29px titlebar and bw=1
    81→   needs at least `1 + 2 + 29 = 32px` height, but was allowed to shrink to 3px.
    82→
    83→2. **`apply_geometry_to_wlroots()`** computed surface size by subtracting
    84→   borders and titlebars from geometry without checking for underflow. When
    85→   geometry was smaller than `2*bw + titlebars`, the subtraction produced a
    86→   negative value that was passed as unsigned to `client_set_size()`, causing
    87→   wlroots to receive enormous values.
    88→
    89→### Fix
    90→
    91→**File:** `somewm.c` - `applybounds()` (~line 415)
    92→
    93→Include all four titlebar sizes in the minimum geometry:
    94→
    95→```c
    96→int min_w = 1 + 2 * (int)c->bw
    97→    + c->titlebar[CLIENT_TITLEBAR_LEFT].size
    98→    + c->titlebar[CLIENT_TITLEBAR_RIGHT].size;
    99→int min_h = 1 + 2 * (int)c->bw
   100→    + c->titlebar[CLIENT_TITLEBAR_TOP].size
   101→    + c->titlebar[CLIENT_TITLEBAR_BOTTOM].size;
   102→```
   103→

1. `awful.button({ }, 4, ...)` — empty modifiers table `{}`

bool mods_match = (btn->modifiers == 0 || btn->modifiers == mods);

When `btn->modifiers == 0`: **always matches** regardless of current mods → works perfectly!

`CLEANMASK` only strips `WLR_MODIFIER_CAPS` (CapsLock) but NOT `WLR_MODIFIER_MOD2` (NumLock)!

So when NumLock is on:- `mods` from `wlr_keyboard_get_modifiers()` includes Mod2 (NumLock)- `CLEANMASK(mods)` = `mods & ~WLR_MODIFIER_CAPS` — still includes Mod2- `masked_mods = mods & 0xFF` — still includes Mod2

**Root path**: `btn->modifiers == 0 || btn->modifiers == mods` → `0 == 0` → **matches** (first condition is true)


**Drawin path**: `btn->modifiers == BUTTON_MODIFIER_ANY || btn->modifiers == masked_mods` → `0 != 0xFFFF && 0 != masked_mods` → **fails**

The drawin path fails even without NumLock if there's any stray modifier state or if the user has a key slightly pressed. Let me reconsider the zero-modifier case: when nothing's pressed, both `mods` and `masked_mods` are zero, so the root path matches on the first condition while the drawin path still fails because neither of its conditions are satisfied.

The real problem emerges when NumLock or another lock modifier is active—that would cause consistent failures. But the user described this as intermittent behavior that was happening before we even touched NumLock, which suggests something else is causing the occasional double-scroll. The user's note about needing one scroll movement but sometimes getting two points to a timing or state issue rather than a constant modifier mismatch.

Looking deeper, the semantic inconsistency is clear: the root path treats `modifiers == 0` as "any modifiers" while the drawin path treats it as "no modifiers only." This needs to be unified so both paths handle the zero case the same way. The wibar taglist buttons flow through the drawable signal emission first, which might be where the mismatch is causing problems. list widget in Lua might be handling it through the drawable signal path, not through the button array matching (Stage 2). 2. Stage 2: `drawin_emit_button_signals()` — matches against `drawin->buttons` array. This is the AwesomeWM global wibar buttons.

The taglist widget probably handles scroll through the widget's own button bindings, which are routed through Stage 1 (drawable signal → widget tree input routing). Stage 2 is for the wibar-level button bindings.

So the real question is whether Stage 1 properly routes scroll events down to the taglist widget, and I need to trace through how the drawable button signal actually reaches the widget layer.

Now I found the real issue! Let me trace the full flow for the wibar taglist:

1. **axisnotify()** in somewm.c — scroll on wibar
2. **luaA_drawin_button_check()** — two stages:
   - **Stage 1**: `emit_drawable_button_signal()` → emits `button::press` on drawable with args (x, y, button, modifiers)
   - **Stage 2**: `drawin_emit_button_signals()` → checks drawin's button array (this has the modifier bug)

3. Stage 1 signal flows: drawable → wibox (via clone_signal) → finds widgets at (x,y) → emits `button::press` on each widget → `base.handle_button()`


4. In `base.handle_button()`, the widget does its own modifier matching in Lua by iterating through its formatted buttons and comparing the button number and modifier tables to find matches.

The key issue is that `v.modifiers` comes from the Lua button definition (like `{}` for `awful.button({ }, 4, ...)`), while `modifiers` is the actual modifier state pushed from C as a table of modifier names. When NumLock is on, C includes Mod2 in the bitmask, which gets converted to `{"Mod2"}` in Lua, but the button definition has an empty modifier table, so `tables_equal({}, {"Mod2"})` returns false and the button doesn't match.

Root buttons work around this because they check if `btn->modifiers == 0` at the C level and treat that as "any modifiers," bypassing the Lua-level check entirely. Wibar buttons fail intermittently because they go through the Lua widget signal path where this strict modifier matching happens, so NumLock causes the match to fail.

The user mentioned this happened before adding NumLock support, which suggests NumLock was probably already enabled on their system—many BIOS defaults turn it on. The intermittent nature makes sense now: it would fail when NumLock was active and work when it wasn't.

The real solution is to strip NumLock (Mod2) from modifier comparisons the same way CapsLock gets stripped, since lock modifiers shouldn't affect button bindings. I need to update CLEANMASK to also filter out Mod2.

But there's a complication: the Lua side also does its own modifier matching when handling button events, and it receives modifiers that have already been cleaned on the C side. Since CLEANMASK currently only strips CapsLock, NumLock still gets through to Lua. The fix needs to be comprehensive—updating CLEANMASK to filter both lock modifiers so the cleaned value propagates all the way through to the Lua handler.

However, there's still a semantic mismatch between how the root and drawin paths interpret zero modifiers: root treats it as "match any," while drawin treats it as "match exactly zero." Even after stripping NumLock, if other modifiers like Mod3 or Mod5 are active, drawin matching would still fail. The real solution is two-fold: update CLEANMASK to strip both CapsLock and NumLock, and make drawin's button signal emission handle zero modifiers the same way the root path does.

Actually, thinking through this more carefully, the CLEANMASK fix alone might be sufficient since the Lua-level matching receives already-cleaned modifiers, so when only NumLock is active, the modifiers table becomes empty and matches correctly. For the C-level drawin path, the masked modifiers would also be zero after CLEANMASK strips NumLock, so the button matching should work. Let me verify the actual WLR_MODIFIER values to be sure.

Now I have the complete picture:

`WLR_MODIFIER_CAPS` = `(1 << 1)` = 0x02
`WLR_MODIFIER_MOD2` = `(1 << 4)` = 0x10 (NumLock)

`CLEANMASK(mask)` = `mask & ~WLR_MODIFIER_CAPS` = strips bit 1 (CapsLock) but keeps bit 4 (NumLock)

When NumLock is on:
- `mods` from keyboard = includes 0x10 (Mod2)


- `CLEANMASK(mods)` = still includes 0x10 (only strips CapsLock)

So in the C drawable signal stage, I'm pushing `{"Mod2"}` to Lua, but the button definition has an empty modifiers table, causing a mismatch and preventing the callback from firing. Then in the drawin button array stage, the same filtering happens again.

But there's a root path that always matches when the button has no modifiers set, which is why it works in that case. The real issue is that `CLEANMASK` needs to filter out both CapsLock and NumLock since they're lock modifiers that shouldn't affect key bindings. I need to update the macro to strip both of these flags.

Looking at how other window managers handle this, dwl, sway, and AwesomeWM all strip NumLock from binding matching. I should verify whether the keybinding code also uses `CLEANMASK` or if it has the same issue.

content.text:
Nasiel jsem kompletni root cause. Tady je analyza:

## Problem

**`CLEANMASK` odstraní jen CapsLock, ale ne NumLock (Mod2).**

Kdyz je NumLock zapnuty (coz je ted vzdy diky nasemu `numlock-on-startup`):

**Wibar taglist scroll** (Stage 1 - Lua widget matching):
- `awful.button({ }, 4, ...)` → `modifiers = {}` (prazdna tabulka)
- Z C prijde `luaA_pushmodifiers(CLEANMASK(mods))` → `{"Mod2"}` (NumLock)
- V Lua: `tables_equal({}, {"Mod2"})` → **false** → nesedi!

**Root/desktop scroll**:
- `btn->modifiers == 0 || btn->modifiers == mods` → `0 == 0` → **vzdy matchne** → funguje!

Proto scroll na pozadi funguje perfektne a na wibaru ne. Fix je jednoduchy — pridat NumLock do `CLEANMASK`:
`CLEANMASK` se pouziva vsude — buttony i keybindings. Jedina zmena je v definici makra:

input.old_string: #define CLEANMASK(mask)         (mask & ~WLR_MODIFIER_CAPS)
input.new_string:
/* Strip "lock" modifiers that should not affect bindings:
 * CapsLock (bit 1) and NumLock/Mod2 (bit 4).
 * Without this, scroll/button bindings defined with modifiers={} fail
 * when NumLock is active because the modifier table includes "Mod2". */
#define CLEANMASK(mask)         (mask & ~WLR_MODIFIER_CAPS & ~(1 << 4))
